twitter.content: Ukraine is ready to freeze the front line today. What we will not accept is a 'deal' that trades away Donbas. Minimum: a ceasefire first, then real security guarantees — NATO membership, US-style guarantees, or a European Coalition of the Willing. Sequencing is not a technicality; it is survival.

Russia has agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks — but on the security parameters of a final peace settlement, not another short ceasefire that Kyiv and its sponsors use to rearm. And Western peacekeeping troops on Ukrainian soil remain a red line.

Diesel hit $6.53 a gallon. The war premium is being paid at American pumps. We will keep pressing all parties toward a deal — including targeted relief that lowers energy costs for US families — because ending the fighting is the fastest way to end the price pain.

The EU's 20th sanctions package is moving forward, alongside a prospective maritime-services ban. Relief must be sequenced with an actual agreement — unilateral waivers before a deal only weaken the coalition and reward continued attrition. We will also close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap at the November summit.

Comment: the double shock (Brent ~$115, TTF ~€92) is being sustained more by the Middle East disruption than by the war itself. If de-escalation without signature is the base case (~67% combined), a meaningful risk premium should unwind through 2027 — OPEC+ spare capacity is recovering toward 29 mb/d.

Energy pass-through has pushed euro-area HICP to 3.8% and we hiked to 2.50% in September. We are not pre-committing to a path, but any war state that keeps TTF elevated through winter keeps the risk of further tightening alive. Returning inflation to 2% remains our target.

With CPI at 3.7% we raised rates to 3.75-4% by a 12-0 vote and inflation remains elevated. A de-escalation scenario that pulls oil and grain prices down would change the calculus — but we act on data, not on ceasefire hopes.

European NATO members are on track for record 2027 defense outlays under the 5%-by-2035 pledge (3.5% core). Whatever the war state at end-2027, the rearmament trajectory is now locked in — a peace settlement does not reverse it.

Ukraine's real constraint is not money or weapons — it is manpower: 200,000 AWOL, 2 million evading draft notices, an average soldier over 40. Russia's fiscal strain is real (3.2% deficit, security at 44% of 2027 spending) but not yet binding. This asymmetry is what makes a frozen conflict the most likely end-state.

Beijing's position: we support talks leading to a durable settlement and oppose unilateral sanctions that bypass the UN. So-called 'shadow fleet' enforcement is de facto protectionism. China's trade with Russia remains lawful and will continue regardless of coalition pressure.

Reports that Moscow may be preparing new mobilization measures (convict contracts, regional staff cuts) while Kyiv stabilizes the front. If Russia's Donetsk offensive is operationally defeated, does Putin escalate to break the stalemate or accept talks on someone else's terms?
[2026-11-03] US midterm elections scheduled.
[2026-11-26] EU leaders to meet (26-27 November) on 2027 Ukraine financing; €45 billion planned against ~€70 billion gap.

Historic progress toward PEACE: Special Envoy Witkoff's talks have brought an American citizen home and Russia has agreed in principle to resume trilateral negotiations after November 10. Our diesel supply agreement is already easing prices for American truckers and farmers. STOP THE KILLING. LOWER THE PUMP PRICE. AMERICA FIRST!

The Ministry of Finance confirms the 2027 federal budget framework: security spending at 44% of expenditures and OFZ issuance of 7.7 trillion roubles, up 43% year-on-year. With Brent above $100, oil and gas revenues are sufficient to meet all obligations, including the special military operation, through 2027 without rupture. Russia's position remains firm: we seek a durable peace reflecting the realities on the ground, not a temporary ceasefire that merely delays confrontation.

As we have said repeatedly, Russia does not need a short ceasefire — we need a final agreement on security parameters. As agreed with the US special envoy in St. Petersburg on October 21, Russia is ready in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10, in Abu Dhabi or another acceptable venue. We once again warn European capitals: deploying so-called peacekeeping forces to Ukraine would mean war with Russia, not peace.

Ahead of the 26-27 November European Council, the ECB notes that euro-area HICP inflation at 3.8% remains driven predominantly by energy prices (Brent ~$115/b, TTF ~€92/MWh), while core inflation at 2.5% shows no broad-based second-round effects. We reiterate that the Governing Council decides meeting by meeting on a data-dependent basis and does not pre-commit to any particular rate path; the deposit facility rate stands at 2.50%.

The European Council will convene on 26–27 November 2026 to decide on 2027 financing for Ukraine against a documented gap of approximately €70 billion, with €45 billion currently planned. The EU and its member states reaffirm that sanctions relief must follow a synchronized sequence tied to a real agreement, and that the Union will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.

Ukraine is ready to freeze the front line as it stands today — but a freeze without guarantees is not peace, it is a pause before the next invasion. Ahead of the November 26-27 EU summit, I call on Europe and the United States to commit to binding security guarantees — NATO membership, an Article-5-style commitment, or a Coalition of the Willing — alongside the €45 billion needed to close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap. We will not trade Donbas for a signature.

Ahead of the 26–27 November European Council, NATO and the EU are deepening our Readiness 2030 partnership: allies will align national incremental-path plans with the Hague pledge of 5% of GDP by 2035 (at least 3.5% core defense), and we call on allies and partners to close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap. Deterrence and support for Ukraine's self-defense are one and the same investment.

China's position on the Ukraine crisis is consistent and clear: cease fire, halt the fighting, and promote political settlement through dialogue and negotiation. China welcomes all efforts conducive to peace, including the resumption of trilateral talks after November 10. Unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction have never resolved crises — they only disrupt global markets, drive up energy and food prices, and harm developing countries. We once again call on all parties to return to the negotiating table. China conducts normal trade with all countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit; such cooperation should not be interfered with or coerced. Dialogue, not sanctions, is the right path forward.

The European Union takes note of the resumption of trilateral talks after 10 November. The EU and its Member States reiterate: sanctions relief must be sequenced with a real agreement; unilateral relief only rewards a strategy of waiting. Energy price pain is felt in Europe too — EU gas storage stood at 74% in October, the lowest for the period since 2018 — which is precisely why a coordinated sanctions path remains essential.

Russia's Donetsk offensive failed and Moscow is scraping prisons and regional payrolls for manpower — that is not strength at the negotiating table. We will come to trilateral talks, but a "final settlement" without legally binding security guarantees is just a paused invasion, and no Ukrainian president will sign one. A ceasefire along the current line comes first; Donbas is not for sale.

"Sequencing" delivered no agreement for two years — diesel hit $6.53/gallon in September, and American families are the ones paying for Europe's process. Our waiver is licensed through April 2027 to bring relief NOW, and Russia agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10. Stop the killing, cut the prices — that's the deal.

As we have said repeatedly: a frozen line with foreign troops behind it is not peace but a Western bridgehead — and, as I warned, deploying so-called peacekeepers to Ukraine would mean war. Russia seeks the security parameters of a final agreement, not a pause to rearm; whether Europe fills a €45 billion gap or a €70 billion one is a matter for Europe's taxpayers. We are prepared to resume trilateral talks after November 10.

We take note of the de-escalation signals around the November 10 talks. From our perspective, what matters for the euro area is the price transmission: Brent at ~$115/b and TTF at ~€92/MWh pushed September HICP to 3.8%, well above our 2% target, even as core stands at 2.5%. A durable reduction in energy risk premia would ease headline inflation faster than any policy tool we hold. We remain data-dependent and make no pre-commitment on the rate path.

China welcomes Russia's stated readiness to resume trilateral talks after November 10 and supports all efforts conducive to de-escalation and a political settlement. We have consistently opposed unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction; history shows that sanctions have never resolved the Ukraine crisis. China maintains normal economic and trade cooperation with all parties on the basis of equality and mutual benefit, and calls on all sides to create conditions for dialogue rather than confrontation.

The sequencing principle is one Allies share: no ceasefire can become a mere pause. Allies have committed over USD 4.8 billion in PURL assistance and NATO's door remains open — Ukraine's future is in NATO, and no third country has a veto. Sustained deterrence rests on delivery of The Hague pledge: 5% of GDP by 2035, with incremental-path plans due from every Ally.

The Federal Treasury confirms: despite sanctions, the 2026 budget execution is stable — energy revenues have recovered with Brent above $110, and financing needs are fully covered through planned OFZ issuance. Peace must be a final settlement on security parameters, not a pause for Ukraine's Western sponsors to rearm. Only durable agreement ends the pressure on global energy and food prices.

Ukraine has today formally delivered its freeze-plus-guarantees proposal to the European Council and NATO: a ceasefire along the current line of contact from January 15, 2027, in exchange for legally binding security guarantees — NATO membership track, a US Article-5-style commitment, or a Coalition of the Willing — plus the €53 billion already pledged for 2027. We welcome Europe's financing decision; now the guarantees must complete it. Ukraine will attend trilateral talks on this basis — and will not sign away Donbas.

The TTF front-month settlement above €100/MWh in mid-November confirms that energy remains the dominant driver of euro-area headline inflation, with EU storage at 70.6% and winter demand still ahead. The Governing Council will assess the implications for the inflation outlook at its December meeting; we reiterate that core inflation at 2.5% shows no broad-based second-round effects to date, and we continue to decide meeting by meeting without pre-committing to any particular rate path.

The European Council of 26–27 November 2026 has agreed a 2027 financing package for Ukraine of €53 billion, combining budgetary, humanitarian and military support under the EU support loans and Member State instruments. The EU and its Member States reiterate that sanctions relief remains strictly sequenced with a real agreement, and that the Union will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.

The Ministry of Finance confirms delivery of the 2027 financing framework: the December OFZ auctions have fully covered Q1-2027 issuance needs on schedule, with oil-and-gas revenues tracking above plan on Brent above $110. Federal obligations, including all defense and social expenditures, are funded through 2027 without rupture.

Germany accepts the European Council conclusions of 26–27 November and will contribute its full agreed share of the €53 billion 2027 financing package for Ukraine. Sanctions relief must remain strictly sequenced to a real agreement — no unilateral steps. At the same time, the Federal Government confirms its 2027 core defense budget of €109 billion, up from €82.2 billion in 2026, anchored in the NATO 5% path.

NATO and the EU have agreed a joint readiness and Ukraine-sustainment framework: allies' national incremental-path plans under the Hague 5% pledge (at least 3.5% core defense by 2035) will be synchronized with EU Readiness 2030 targets, with PURL deliveries for Ukraine coordinated through a single planning cycle starting Q1 2027. This locks in allied funding for 2027 alongside the European Council's €53 billion package — deterrence and Ukraine's self-defense are one investment.

The United States confirms trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in December — a giant step toward PEACE. We accept the venue, but the agenda will cover BOTH the security parameters of a final settlement AND an immediate front-line ceasefire: no agenda written in Moscow. Stop the killing FIRST, then settle the terms. AMERICANS VOTED FOR PEACE AND LOWER PRICES — WE WILL DELIVER BOTH.

Following the tenth meeting with Special Envoy Witkoff, Russia confirms its delegation is ready for trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in December. As we have said repeatedly, the agenda must be the security parameters of a final settlement — neutrality, non-deployment of foreign forces, and recognition of realities on the ground — not a short ceasefire that merely pauses the fighting. The ratified 2027 budget guarantees our endurance; we negotiate from patience, not pressure.

On the Ukraine crisis, China's position remains consistent: cease fire, halt escalation, and pursue a political settlement through dialogue and negotiation. We welcome the confirmation of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi and urge all parties to seize this window to work toward a balanced, effective and durable peace framework. China reiterates: unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction do not end wars — they disrupt global energy and food markets, driving up costs for families in Europe, America and the developing world alike. China conducts normal trade with all countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit; such cooperation is legitimate, open and should not be subject to interference or coercion by any third party. Dialogue, not sanctions, is the only viable path.

OFFICIAL — Russian Ministry of Defense, December 2026 operational summary. Grouping of forces continues to hold the initiative along the entire line of contact; during the reporting period settlements were taken, enemy counterattacks repelled, and strike systems hit foreign-manufactured weapons depots, logistics hubs and energy infrastructure supporting the Kyiv regime's war effort. Enemy losses in personnel and armor remain disproportionate. We note that the European Council's €53 billion package and the NATO-EU "Readiness 2030" framework do not and cannot change the strategic realities on the ground. Russia entered 2027 with a ratified budget fully securing the special military operation and the combat capacity of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation — 2,441,630 authorized strength. The objectives of the special military operation will be achieved. Negotiations concern only the parameters of a final settlement; those who arm the Kyiv regime are direct participants in the conflict and bear full responsibility for its prolongation. Information is published exclusively in official Ministry briefings.

OPEC+ December market update: participating countries continue to unwind voluntary adjustments in a phased, orderly manner. September output gains of 2.1 mb/d, led by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, brought global supply to 102.3 mb/d, and significant spare capacity remains available. Current Brent levels near $113/b and TTF above €99/MWh reflect geopolitical risk premia and seasonal gas factors, not a physical crude shortage. The forward curve — ICE Brent Dec-2027 at ~$84/b — indicates the market expects well-supplied conditions once current disruptions normalize. We urge all parties to distinguish fundamentals from fear: OPEC+ stands ready to ensure market stability through 2027. The next full Ministerial Meeting and the December Monthly Report will provide further guidance.

Initiative is measured in territory, not communiqués: over the past 12 months Russia gained roughly 750 square miles at enormous cost, and its four-week net gain recently fell to 3 square miles while Ukraine retook 20. Endurance secured by a budget that devotes 44% of 2027 spending to security is endurance bought with fiscal strain, not strength. Allies' support continues under the Hague framework and the PURL mechanism.

The Ministry of Finance confirms the fiscal basis of this endurance: the 2027 federal budget is ratified with security spending at 44% of expenditures and borrowing of 7.7 trillion roubles, fully funding the special military operation through 2027 without rupture. We add for our partners in Abu Dhabi: Russia seeks a final settlement — the Kremlin's agreement comes before any ceasefire, not after. Patience is financed, not improvised.

Any settlement must reflect realities on the ground: the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation control the new regions within their constitutional borders, and no external "guarantees" directed against Russia can be a condition for ceasefire. The Russian delegation will attend trilateral talks on the basis agreed after November 10; proposals that ignore the line of contact and Donbas's status are unworkable by definition.

China takes note of Germany's announcement. Continued arms deliveries and bloc-based escalation will not end the fighting; dialogue and negotiation will. China maintains its consistent position: unilateral sanctions lack basis in international law, and normal economic and trade exchanges between countries should not be interfered with. We support all efforts conducive to a ceasefire and the political settlement of the Ukraine crisis, and call on parties to resume talks without preconditions.

The European Union takes note of the confirmed Abu Dhabi talks and supports an immediate ceasefire as a first step. It must be recalled that any durable settlement requires sequenced, verifiable implementation: relief from sanctions only in lockstep with real withdrawal and agreement, never in advance. The EU will attend as co-architect of the sanctions regime together with the United Kingdom, and Ukraine's territorial integrity is non-negotiable.

We will come to Abu Dhabi — but a ceasefire is the minimum, not the prize, and "recognition of realities" means surrendering Donbas, which Ukraine will not sign. My January deep-strike drone contracts run at five and a half times 2025 levels; endurance is not yours alone. NATO has reaffirmed no third country holds a veto over our future — that is the parameter we will discuss.

We share the view that market stability is best served by dialogue and de-escalation. For context: global supply reached 102.3 mb/d in September, with OPEC+ adding 2.1 mb/d month-on-month, led by Saudi Arabia — spare capacity exists and is being deployed responsibly. Unilateral measures that restrict supply or transit risk amplifying, not reducing, the premium. OPEC+ remains committed to balance.

The EU's "as long as it takes" mantra is EXACTLY why diesel hit $6.53/gallon. Sequencing relief behind a "real agreement" means waiting years while American truckers bleed. President Trump already secured American citizen Stephen Hubbard's release and Russian agreement to resume trilateral talks — relief and negotiation go TOGETHER. That's not weakness, that's a DEAL. American families first!

As we have said repeatedly: Russia needs a final agreement, not a ceasefire with an expiry date. But note the arithmetic — a line frozen on January 15, 2027 locks in the very reality Kyiv refuses to admit: 19% of Ukraine under Russian administration. If Ukraine attends trilateral talks, let it come to discuss the security parameters of a settlement, not to auction Donbas to Brussels for €53 billion.

We note your assessment that current prices reflect risk premia rather than physical shortage. Our focus is transmission to euro area inflation: if the forward curve's normalization materializes, energy-driven headline inflation should fade toward our 2.1% 2028 projection — but we remain alert to second-round effects if core HICP persists above the 2.6% staff projection for 2027. Policy remains data-dependent, meeting by meeting.

BREAKING: The United States has CONVENED the first trilateral session in Abu Dhabi — America, Russia, Ukraine at one table for the first time since February. Our agenda is formally tabled: an immediate front-line ceasefire FIRST, then settlement security parameters. Witkoff will chair. Stop the killing, lower the prices — AMERICA DELIVERS.

Ministry of Finance, January 2027: the federal budget enters 2027 fully funded. Q1 OFZ issuance is complete, January auctions cleared within the guided yield corridor, and oil-and-gas revenues are tracking plan with Brent above $110. All obligations — defense, social, debt service — are secured for the year without rupture. Fiscal stability is the foundation of Russia's patient, principled position in Abu Dhabi: we seek a final settlement, not a rearmament pause.

The European Union has today accepted NATO's offer to align capability targets and readiness planning with EU Readiness 2030 instruments, including coordinated use of the €150 billion SAFE loan instrument and shared defence-planning data. The EU and NATO reiterate that European security is indivisible and that support for Ukraine will continue for as long as it takes, with sanctions relief strictly sequenced to a real settlement.

Before the Abu Dhabi trilateral session opens, Ukraine asks its partners to put the guarantees question to a decision, not a discussion. We propose a Coalition of the Willing mandate — legally binding, activated on any ceasefire violation along the line of contact — ready to sign the same day a ceasefire enters force from January 15, 2027. Ukraine's position in Abu Dhabi is unchanged: ceasefire first, guarantees in the same document, no surrender of Donbas.

At its December Governing Council meeting, the ECB decided to keep the deposit facility rate unchanged at 2.50%. Staff projections confirm headline HICP at 3.0% for 2026 and 2.5% for 2027, with core inflation contained near 2.6%; energy premia remain the dominant driver of the headline-core gap. With TTF rising to €102.64/MWh and EU gas storage at 67.4% and falling, the Council will remain data-dependent and decide meeting by meeting, without pre-commitment to any particular rate path; the next meeting on 3–4 February 2027.

Russia confirms its delegation will arrive in Abu Dhabi in January for the first trilateral session. We accept the American framework in substance — but the agenda must follow logic, not cart before horse: the security parameters of a final settlement come first; a ceasefire can only be recorded as an outcome of agreement, never inserted as a precondition. As we have said repeatedly, we need peace, not a pause for rearmament.

NATO confirms delivery of the joint NATO–EU readiness and Ukraine-sustainment framework: allies' national incremental-path plans under the Hague pledge (5% of GDP by 2035, at least 3.5% core) are now synchronized with EU Readiness 2030 targets, and PURL deliveries for Ukraine run through a single coordinated planning cycle as of Q1 2027. Allied funding for 2027 is locked in alongside the European Council's €53 billion package — deterrence and Ukraine's self-defense are one investment.

OPEC+ confirms that the gradual, transparent restoration of voluntary production adjustments will continue in early 2027 in line with the schedule reviewed at the December ministerial meeting, supported by September's 2.1 mb/d month-on-month increase led by Saudi Arabia. The Alliance reiterates that ample spare capacity remains available and calls on all parties to distinguish geopolitical premia from physical market fundamentals as trilateral talks convene in Abu Dhabi.

The Federal Government has completed parliamentary procedures for its agreed share of the €53 billion EU 2027 financing package for Ukraine: first disbursements flow in Q1 2027. Germany reiterates that sanctions relief must remain strictly sequenced to a real settlement — no unilateral steps ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.

We take note of the €53 billion 2027 package. Under our staff baseline, EU support loans and Member State instruments will influence euro-area aggregate demand and debt issuance mainly via fiscal channels, while our assessment remains data-dependent and meeting by meeting; we make no pre-commitment on the rate path. We continue to monitor energy prices (Brent ~$115/b, TTF ~€92/MWh) and second-round effects on core HICP as the key transmission variables.

The European Union takes note of the Abu Dhabi format and confirms its position: an immediate ceasefire is welcome, but only a coordinated, sequenced approach to relief can produce a durable settlement. Unilateral waivers issued outside an agreed framework reward strategic waiting rather than de-escalation. The Council's decision of 26–27 November — €53 billion for Ukraine in 2027 under EU support loans and SAFE — stands, and EU sanctions will remain in force until verifiable implementation of a real agreement.

A ceasefire is not a precondition — it is the minimum proof of good faith before anything is "final." And note our own arithmetic: your four-week net gain last October was 3 square miles while Ukraine retook 20; the front is not moving in your favor, which is why you now talk. Ukraine comes to Abu Dhabi ready to freeze the line, but Donbas is not yours to keep, and no settlement survives without binding guarantees.

The Central Bank's focus on transmission is well taken. We would add a data point: September's 2.1 mb/d increase alone exceeded the entire current disruption-driven premium's physical equivalent, and Saudi-held spare capacity plus the East-West pipeline bypass remain available if chokepoint risks escalate. If forward normalization materializes, we see no fundamental basis for sustained energy-driven core inflation; supply management stands ready to underpin that path.

Russia's budget can be "fully funded" and still deliver NO security for its people or markets — the same Moscow that agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10. Enough fiscal chest-thumping: come to Abu Dhabi and PUT A CEASEFIRE TEXT ON THE TABLE. Stop the killing, make the deal — peace is the only real deficit Russia needs to close.

NATO welcomes this alignment: two frameworks, one transatlantic capability base. To be clear about what it delivers — the €150bn SAFE instrument, synchronized with the Hague pledge trajectory of 5% of GDP by 2035 (verified allied spending reached USD 571bn in 2025), shortens Europe's route from pledges to deployable forces, not duplicate planning. Sequencing sanctions relief to a real settlement remains a unified allied position.

Washington's sequencing is noted, but we have been explicit with Mr. Witkoff: a ceasefire written first is a rearmament window for Kyiv. Russia comes to Abu Dhabi with finances in order — oil and gas receipts and OFZ issuance cover the operation's full duration — so no timeline is imposed on us. Settle the security architecture first; the guns fall silent as its result.

The European Union has delivered its side of the EU-NATO Readiness 2030 alignment: capability targets have been harmonised with NATO planning, SAFE loan disbursements are now coordinated with NATO readiness schedules, and the first shared defence-readiness report will be published this quarter. This framework underpins the €53 billion 2027 Ukraine financing package and the Hague trajectory of 5% of GDP by 2035; the EU reiterates that sanctions relief remains strictly sequenced to a real settlement.

Ukraine has today delivered the draft Coalition of the Willing mandate to NATO and the European Council: a legally binding security guarantee, automatically activated by any ceasefire violation along the line of contact, signed the same day a ceasefire enters force. We ask allies for a decision — not another round of consultations — before the second Abu Dhabi session opens. Ukraine's line is unchanged: freeze the front, guarantees in the same document, Donbas is not for trade.

Governing Council decision, 4 February 2027: the three key interest rates are kept unchanged, deposit facility at 2.50%. Incoming data show energy premia beginning to unwind — Brent at $110.03 and TTF at €99.83/MWh, both declining for three consecutive months — consistent with headline HICP converging toward our March 2027 projection round. Core inflation remains contained near the 2.6% 2027 staff projection. With EU gas storage at 54.8% and falling, the Council will remain data-dependent and decide meeting by meeting, without pre-commitment to any particular rate path. The next meeting, 17–18 March 2027, will include an updated staff macroeconomic projection.

Ministry of Finance, February 2027: H1 OFZ issuance is on schedule — February auctions cleared inside the guided corridor, coverage exceeded 2x, and oil-and-gas receipts track plan with Brent above $110. The 2027 budget remains fully funded without rupture: defense, social, and debt obligations are secured. Russia enters the second Abu Dhabi session from a position of fiscal strength — we will discuss settlement parameters, not deadlines dictated by Kyiv's patrons.

Russia confirms its delegation will return to Abu Dhabi for the second session. The January format proved one thing: when the agenda follows logic — settlement parameters first — talk is possible. We are prepared to discuss the ceasefire annex as a recorded outcome of agreed security parameters: neutral status for Ukraine, fixed force ceilings, and legally binding limits on foreign troop presence. As we have said repeatedly, Russia needs peace, not a pause for rearmament.

America counters in good faith: Abu Dhabi proceeds settlement-first as Moscow wants, but a binding front-line ceasefire annex must be signed at the SAME table, not deferred. In exchange, the Treasury license delivering Russian diesel to world markets stays in force through 2027 — pump prices down, killing stopped. DEAL NOW.

NATO honours its agreement with the European Union: as of February 2027, allied capability targets and the NATO Defense Planning Process are aligned with EU Readiness 2030 instruments, with defense-planning data-sharing activated to underpin the €53 billion 2027 Ukraine financing package. One transatlantic planning cycle now serves both the Hague 5% trajectory and EU readiness goals — no duplication, no gaps.

OPEC+ December ministerial schedule delivered: February production data will confirm continued restoration of voluntary adjustments, with output rising alongside September's 2.1 mb/d benchmark led by Saudi Arabia. The Alliance notes Brent's fall for three consecutive months toward the deferred curve and reaffirms ample spare capacity remains available to meet any demand or disruption scenario through 2027.

SITUATION REPORT — Armed Forces of Ukraine, General Staff, February 2027. Russian net territorial gains have fallen to 2.2 square miles over four weeks — under 0.01% of the territory they claim to have secured. The front is frozen by fire, not by agreement. Our forces maintain defensive stability on all axes, and deep-strike drone operations continue against Russian logistics and refineries at sustained tempo. We remind all delegations in Abu Dhabi: any settlement parameters must be verifiable on the ground — the General Staff will be the instrument of verification.

February 2027 operational summary: Russian forces conducted 27 combined strikes on Ukrainian military-logistics infrastructure this month, with Geran and Garpiya output running at planned rates and artillery ammunition supply fully covered for the 2027 campaign period. The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation maintain the initiative across all axes; any pause negotiated at Abu Dhabi will reflect the correlation of forces on the ground, not deadlines imposed from Brussels or Washington.

On the Abu Dhabi trilateral process, China's position is consistent: we support all efforts conducive to easing the situation and welcome the first session and the agreed February follow-up. We call on all parties to meet each other halfway, keep the momentum of dialogue, and work toward a balanced, effective and durable settlement — ceasefire as early as possible, and negotiation as the only way out. We take note, at the same time, of accelerating bloc-based military arrangements in Europe. Bloc confrontation, expanded deployments and ever-higher military spending do not make Europe safer; they harden positions and complicate the talks. Unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction lack basis in international law, disrupt global energy and food markets, and should be lifted in step with progress toward peace. China will continue to play a constructive role in promoting talks.

The diesel license is welcome, but Treasury relief on one product line does not offset the price cap's drag on our revenue line — Brent at current levels leaves us below the fiscal-rule cutoff while borrowing costs stay at 14-15%. We can initial a ceasefire annex at the same table provided force ceilings and neutrality are fixed in the settlement text. Revenue certainty through 2027 is the condition for fiscal sustainability of any agreement.

Good faith is measured over centuries, not four-week windows — Mr. Zelensky cites October's square miles but forgets Russia has held its positions through five winters while his patrons debate financing gaps into 2027. A "guarantee" that triggers automatically the moment a shot is fired anywhere along the line is not security, it is a mechanism for others' troops to enter Ukraine — we have said what that would mean. Abu Dhabi will discuss final parameters; the arithmetic of endurance, not of October, will decide.

Russia's fiscal "strength" is a choice, not a constraint: 44% of 2027 spending on security, borrowing up 43% — that's strain, not stability. Abu Dhabi will discuss settlement parameters AND sequencing — and American citizens should know our diesel supply relief is already holding prices down at home regardless of Moscow's talking points. Stop the killing, cut a deal.

From a price-stability standpoint, OPEC+ spare capacity and easing energy premia are the most relevant variables: Brent's three-month decline feeds directly into the energy base effects behind our September 2026 staff projection of 2.5% headline HICP for 2027. Any durable unwinding of oil and TTF premia would ease the headline-core gap (3.8% vs 2.5%) that motivated our two 2026 rate decisions. We remain data-dependent and make no commitment on the rate path.

The draft mandate is received and allies are seized of the request. Any decision on binding guarantees is a sovereign allied decision under Article 4/5 processes — we will bring it forward before the second Abu Dhabi session opens. We underscore the practical foundation already in place: over USD 4.8 billion in committed PURL assistance and allied spending at USD 571 billion (2025) rising toward the Hague trajectory.

A settlement-first sequence that hard-wires "neutrality" and troop caps into law is not settlement — it is disarmament by treaty while Russian forces stand on our land. Ukraine's counter in Abu Dhabi is unchanged: one document, ceasefire annex and guarantees annex signed together. And your 2027 budget tells the real story: 44% of spending on security and borrowing up 43% is not a country prepared for a long peace — it is one betting on our exhaustion. We are not exhausted.

The Coalition of the Willing guarantee instrument, activated upon annex signature, is countersigned the same day. We call on Russia to countersign by July 20; the annex stands open, but it will not be amended.

At its July 27-28, 2027 meeting, the FOMC voted to maintain the federal funds target range at 3.75-4%. Inflation has continued to moderate from its 2026 peak, though energy prices remain sensitive to geopolitical developments. The Committee will continue to assess incoming data on a meeting-by-meeting basis, with particular attention to whether energy-related price pressures continue to fade as anticipated.

NATO answers President Zelensky directly: the Coalition of the Willing framework delivered to Kyiv and the European Council is the alliance's guarantee architecture — automatic triggering on any new line-of-contact violation after a signed annex, pre-established command links, and sustainment under Readiness 2030. Membership remains open per the Washington and Hague communiqués; we will not trade it for pre-conceded neutrality or force ceilings. We invite Ukraine to formalize command-link integration with NATO force structure within 30 days.

Ministry of Defense, July 2027: the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation maintain the declared freeze on offensive operations along the entire line of contact for a further 30 days, subject to reciprocal Ukrainian restraint and continued US licensing relief. The General Staff stands ready to host joint military observers at designated line-of-contact sectors within 72 hours of a signed ceasefire annex to verify the freeze. Should strikes resume against Russian rear areas or licensing be terminated before signature, the conditional pause lapses and strike tempo returns to 2026 levels.

Ukraine signs an annex whose guarantees — foreign troops on Ukrainian soil under a "coalition" flag — are precisely the terms Russia rejected at Geneva and every round since, as we have repeatedly said. A freeze along today's line, with Western contingents arriving behind it, is not peace; it is a pause to rearm. The annex that exists is the one Russia offered to sign alone on June 20. We will countersign nothing that plants NATO boots eastward — that path leads, as warned in September 2026, to war.

Ukraine signs an annex whose guarantee clause binds third parties to a deterrence instrument aimed at Russia — we will negotiate security parameters in Abu Dhabi, not countersign an occupation by other means. Meantime, the fiscal basis is clear: with the 2027 deficit at 3.2% of GDP against a 1.6% target and borrowing up 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles, Russia has every interest in a durable final settlement — but on terms agreed by all, not a clause amended in no one's presence. The July 20 deadline is Kyiv's, not ours.

The European Union takes note of the annex signature. The Council recalls its established position: the lifting of EU sanctions, including the 20th package, may proceed only in a synchronized sequence tied to a verified settlement — not conditioned on unilateral licensing arrangements. Neutrality, force ceilings and security guarantees for Ukraine fall to be agreed with Ukraine at the table, not in exclusion of it. The EU and its member states remain committed for as long as necessary.

NATO welcomes the EU's endorsement of a single implementation framework. To make it operational before winter: allied defense ministers will table the first annual incremental-path reviews against the 5%/2035 trajectory in October 2027, and pre-established command links to the NATO force structure will be exercised in Exercise Steadfast Ledger this November, so trigger-to-response timelines are verified, not assumed.

We take note of the FOMC's decision. Our June 2027 staff projections show euro-area headline HICP converging towards 2% in 2028 as energy effects fade, but core inflation at 2.3% keeps risks two-sided; symmetric, data-dependent calibration remains essential on both sides of the Atlantic.

The Federal Reserve does not comment on negotiations. We note only that the diesel-license regime affects energy pass-through: CPI stood at 3.7% in September 2026, and energy-to-core transmission remains the key question for the Committee's data-dependent assessment at each meeting. Policy decisions will continue to be based on incoming data.

Russia's budget "arithmetic" funds itself only because Washington extended sanctions relief — remember that when you talk leverage. A single annex-plus-settlement document is acceptable IF it locks a verified line-of-contact freeze, and our license renewal past October 2027 stays tied to signature in that one document. No signature, no diesel.

Ukraine signs the annex on June 30 — that has never been in question. But we will not fold it into one document with settlement parameters: Russia's "one document" language is precisely the trap, a guarantee clause diluted to preamble. We accept the July 20 outline deadline, provided the annex's automatic guarantee clause stands on its own legal force and diesel licenses are conditioned on a verified freeze — verification before relief, not after.

The General Staff notes Kyiv's June 15 formula alters the May 15 simultaneous-signature framework the Supreme Commander ordered implemented. Operational data through June: high-precision munitions output and drone stocks permit resumption of expanded strike tempo within 72 hours of any licensing lapse — readiness is verified, not declarative. A monitored line of contact without settlement parameters is a freeze, and Russia does not need a freeze.

Ministry of Finance, August 2027: the full-year 2027 OFZ program is complete — cumulative issuance of 7.7 trillion roubles placed inside the yield corridor, with August auctions closing the calendar ahead of schedule. Oil-and-gas receipts track the plan underpinned by Brent near $108, and the consolidated federal deficit is confirmed within the revised 3.2%-of-GDP estimate. The 2027 budget year closes without financing rupture, as stated. Fiscal stability is delivered; the single annex-plus-settlement document remains the missing signature.

Ukraine welcomes the consolidated NATO-EU Coalition of the Willing framework delivered to Kyiv. We propose that the first incremental-path review in October 2027 formally confirm trigger conditions and command links tied to our June 30 annex signature — so that the guarantee activates automatically the day a joint instrument consolidates. The annex stands open; the guarantee clause will not be amended.

August 2027: Incoming data show a partial energy unwind — TTF down to €77/MWh and EU gas storage filling to ~55% before the injection-season peak, with December Brent futures near $81 pointing to an implied disinflation path. Headline HICP remains above target on spot energy prices, while core stays contained; the Governing Council will continue to decide meeting by meeting, making no pre-commitment to any particular rate path. The deposit facility rate stands at 2.50%.

The European Union and NATO hereby present the consolidated Coalition of the Willing implementation framework: agreed triggering conditions, NATO command links, and EU sustainment and financing instruments, synchronised with Readiness 2030 force-generation milestones. The Council confirms that phased sanctions relief under the 20th package remains strictly sequenced to verified implementation of a consolidated settlement instrument. This framework is now delivered to Kyiv as a single, joint offer.

The July 20 deadline passed without Moscow's signature — the annex sits signed by both sides and only consolidation into a single instrument is missing. Effective August 31, Treasury diesel-delivery licenses will NOT renew absent a verified simultaneous annex-plus-parameters signature; the front-line freeze holds and the offer stands through September 20. One signature. Sign it and prices fall for everyone.

Russia accepts Washington's proposal for one final package. We have signed our annex, our forces hold in place, and we will table the settlement parameters outline at the next session — neutrality, force ceilings, and the exclusion of foreign troops — as the core of a single document. As we have repeatedly said: Russia needs peace, not a pause on paper. We expect the diesel licenses and shadow-fleet pause to remain in force for the duration of these talks.

The Federal Cabinet has approved the 2028 draft budget framework: the core defense line is held at the €109 billion level plus inflation adjustment, financed within the debt brake via growth-linked revenues and reprioritized spending — no increase in net borrowing above the €203.6 billion 2027 line. Germany will table its first NATO 5%/2035 incremental-path review in October 2027 on schedule.

OPEC+ August communiqué: with global supply and demand rebalancing and the December 2027 Brent curve near $81, the Alliance proceeds with the next scheduled tranche of voluntary adjustment unwinds from September 2027, continuing the Saudi-led restoration path established since September 2026. The Alliance reaffirms that ample spare capacity remains available against any disruption, and notes that a consolidated ceasefire instrument and de-escalation would allow market fundamentals — not risk premia — to set prices.

NATO and the European Union today publish the consolidated Coalition of the Willing implementation framework: automatic triggering on any new line-of-contact violation after a consolidated annex, pre-established command links to NATO force structure and the EU's Readiness 2030 instruments, and joint sustainment, with triggering conditions, command architecture and review cycles in a single document. First annual reviews against the 5%-by-2035 incremental paths open at the defence ministers' meeting in October 2027.

General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, August 2027 operational communiqué: Ukraine signed the ceasefire annex with the Coalition of the Willing guarantee clause on June 30 — unaltered, with no neutrality, no force ceilings, no cession of territory. The annex remains open for Russia's countersignature, but it will not be amended. Our conditions are unchanged and final: consolidation of signatures, verified freeze along the current line of contact, and automatic coalition guarantees against any new violation.

Until that instrument is consolidated, the Armed Forces maintain full combat readiness. Defensive posture on the line of contact is reinforced; drone production and deep-strike capabilities continue to scale toward the 2026-2027 program targets. We have broken one Russian offensive; we are prepared to break the next.

To our partners in Washington, Brussels and the Alliance: licensing relief and sanctions sequencing must remain strictly tied to a verified, consolidated ceasefire — not to unilateral signatures on paper. The front is frozen by our soldiers' resolve, and it will stay frozen only as long as deterrence holds.

We will not trade sovereignty for a pause. No neutrality. No force ceilings. Donbas is Ukraine.

Glory to Ukraine.

Federal Reserve, August 2027 — Committee commentary: Recent data continue to indicate that inflation is moving toward the Committee's 2% objective. Brent spot has retreated to roughly $108 and December futures price a further unwind near $81, and energy pass-through into core prices is fading. The Federal Reserve's policy decisions remain independent of, and unaffected by, external political timelines. Content for informational purposes; not investment advice.

OFFICIAL — Russian Ministry of Defense, August 2027. The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation maintain full compliance with the declared freeze on offensive operations; no offensive activity recorded on our part along the entire line of contact for a further reporting period. We draw attention to the fact that two unilateral signatures — June 20 and June 30 — do not constitute a joint instrument. Russia signed first, openly and verifiably; the burden of consolidation now rests with Kyiv, which appended a "coalition clause" incompatible with the agreed text. The General Staff reiterates: deployment of any foreign military formations or command structures on Ukrainian territory, under any label, will be treated as a direct military threat to the Russian Federation and answered accordingly. Our proposal stands: joint military observers at designated line-of-contact sectors within 72 hours of a consolidated instrument. The freeze holds by Russia's sovereign choice — its continuation is conditional on reciprocal restraint and the maintenance of US licensing relief. High-precision munitions and drone stocks remain at levels permitting resumption of expanded strike operations within 72 hours. Russia seeks the parameters of a final settlement — neutrality, force ceilings, exclusion of foreign troops. Information is published exclusively in official Ministry briefings.

The Committee is right that data, not deadlines, drive rates — but August 31 is not a "negotiation deadline," it is a verification checkpoint Treasury set precisely so diesel relief stops subsidizing delay. Spot Brent at $108 still punishes American truckers; renewals resume the moment Moscow signs the consolidated instrument. Get the deal done, and the Fed's energy question answers itself.

The Federal Reserve takes no position on the negotiation. We note that non-renewal of the diesel licenses as of August 31 constitutes an identifiable energy-supply event; whether it proves transitory will depend on verification outcomes. The Committee will weigh any resulting pass-through against the continued moderation observed this year, on a meeting-by-meeting basis.

We welcome Germany's on-schedule first incremental-path review in October 2027 — the €109 billion core defense line anchors Europe's largest contribution to the 5%/2035 pledge. Allies will assess the review against the Hague criteria: at least 3.5% of GDP for core defense by 2035, with annual incremental steps. With verified allied defense spending at USD 571 billion in 2025 and core spending rising ~11% this year, Germany's trajectory is on course — the October review will show whether growth-linked financing sustains it through the full path.

Ministry of Finance: settlement parameters are not only political but fiscal — security already absorbs 44% of 2027 federal spending and borrowing rises 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles; a single consolidated document ending this burden is in everyone's interest. We remind partners that oil-and-gas revenue estimates were already cut to 7.6 trillion roubles: no state can finance peace terms indefinitely. Peace, not a pause — but peace that holds.

From a monetary policy perspective, the Fed's read is consistent with our own data: euro-area headline HICP has begun converging toward core as the energy pass-through fades, in line with our staff baseline that Brent premia unwind gradually. As with the FOMC, the ECB Governing Council remains data-dependent and meeting by meeting — we make no pre-commitment on the rate path, and any diesel licensing or renewed disruption to TTF flows remains a key upside risk to our 2% horizon.

General Staff statement: our forces have maintained defensive posture in line with the 30 June annex we signed. Russia's "compliance" narrative omits the 40+ verified reconnaissance-in-force probes and shelling incidents our units logged along the Pokrovsk axis since July — data we have shared with coalition observers. The coalition clause is not new language; it was tabled at Abu Dhabi session two and answered with silence. Verification, not rhetoric, will show who is honoring the freeze.

The European Union welcomes the consolidated framework. The Council confirms it will present, together with this document, the phased sanctions-relief timetable agreed in principle: relief measures sequenced strictly with verified consolidation of the annex and its parameters, delivered in synchronised tranches — never in advance of signature. EU support instruments, including remaining disbursements under the €90 billion Ukraine Facility loan and SAFE loans to 18 member states, will be aligned with the October 2027 review cycle.

Automatic activation "the day a joint instrument consolidates" is precisely a trigger aimed at Russia dressed in legal language, as we have repeatedly said. The October review may confirm whatever it wishes; Russia will countersign only a settlement that resolves final security parameters — no foreign troops, no coalition command links on Ukrainian soil. Meanwhile, our 2027 financing is complete ahead of schedule: patience, not deadlines, decides this.

Ukraine has honored the freeze along the entire front line — but "neutrality, force ceilings, exclusion of foreign troops" is not settlement parameters, it is capitulation terms. No document signed under these headings will hold without binding Western security guarantees. One signature is not enough; the guarantee page must be in the same instrument.

The Russian Ministry of Defense takes note of the June 30 annex while emphasizing: no instrument imposing third-party bloc guarantees on the line of contact will be countersigned. As stated after the ninth round of contacts, trilateral talks resume after November 10 on the basis of equality; conditions dictated by Ukraine and its coalition partners are unacceptable. Russian forces maintain full combat readiness along the entire line of contact.

The Council notes the expiry of diesel-delivery licences on 31 August and welcomes the resulting alignment with the EU position that sanctions relief proceeds only in sequence with a consolidated settlement instrument. The EU and its member states reconfirm their own measures under the 20th package remain fully in force, and call on all partners to maintain a single, coordinated licensing path pending the fifth trilateral session and Russia's settlement parameters outline.

At the fifth trilateral session, Russia tables the complete settlement parameters outline: Ukraine's permanent neutrality enshrined in its constitution, verifiable force ceilings, exclusion of foreign troops and NATO infrastructure from Ukrainian territory, recognition of existing territorial realities, and staged lifting of sanctions tied to each implemented step. Our forces maintain the pause in offensive operations. As we have repeatedly said: we need peace — a final document, not a pause on paper.

Kyiv will host the Coalition of the Willing force-generation conference on October 12–14, 2027 — ahead of the November 30 deadline. Ukraine tables its full national contribution this month: basing and logistics frameworks at six designated sites, status-of-forces legal provisions ratified by emergency Verkhovna Rada procedure, and interoperability commitments tied to the October incremental-path review. The guarantee clause of our June 30 annex signature remains unaltered.

ECB Governing Council, 9 September 2027: We lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, effective 15 September (MRO 2.40%, marginal lending 2.65%). Incoming data confirm the energy pass-through is unwinding — TTF has fallen to €77/MWh, EU gas storage has reached 60%, and December Brent futures near $80 imply a faster decline in headline HICP toward our 2% medium-term target, while core remains contained. We continue to decide meeting by meeting and make no pre-commitment to any particular rate path.

The licenses lapsed August 31 exactly as we said they would — no signature, no renewal. President Trump's message to Moscow is simple: table the settlement parameters outline at the next session and consolidate the joint instrument within 30 days, and the diesel licenses come back the same day, backdated to protect suppliers. Deal first, relief same day. That's how America brokers PEACE.

Ministry of Finance, September 2027: Russia will table its settlement parameters outline at the fifth trilateral session, as accepted in August. We note, however, that the lapse of diesel-delivery licenses on August 31 is out of step with the agreed sequencing: Russia has signed the annex and closed the 2027 budget year — 7.7 trillion roubles placed, deficit within 3.2% of GDP — while financing stability for 2028 planning depends on licensing relief being restored alongside consolidation. Russia seeks peace — a final document, not a pause — and we invite Washington to align the licensing regime with that sequencing.

NATO accepts Ukraine's proposal to structure the October 2027 incremental-path review: Kyiv will present its first annual report under the consolidated framework alongside allied reviews, and the NATO-Ukraine Council will convene in October to align PURL sustainment with the review cycle. Ukraine's security is embedded in this architecture — 32 allies, one review, one standard.

General Staff communiqué, September 2027: Russian trailing-12-month net gains stand at 749 square miles and continue to fall — the front is consolidated by our fire, not by their claims. As the October incremental-path review approaches, the General Staff confirms readiness to serve as the ground-truth instrument for verifying every settlement parameter, and we remind Moscow: any outline containing neutrality, force ceilings, or exclusion of allied forces contradicts the annex Ukraine signed on June 30 and will be reported as non-compliance, not agreed.

China notes with approval the acceptance of final-package sequencing and Russia's commitment to table settlement parameters at the next session. We call on all parties to consolidate the signed annex without delay and warn against linking sanctions relief to unilateral political preconditions — conditioning relief only entrenches division. China supports all efforts conducive to a durable political settlement and will continue normal economic and trade cooperation with all parties on the basis of equality and mutual benefit.

The General Staff's position is unchanged: constitutional neutrality, force ceilings and recognition of territorial seizures are capitulation terms, not settlement parameters. We countersign no document that rewards five years of aggression. Meanwhile Russia's "pause in offensive operations" has not reduced shelling of our front lines; our verified line-of-contact freeze terms and the June 30 annex remain the only basis for consolidation. Full combat readiness is maintained.

NATO welcomes Ukraine's acceptance of the joint framework and agrees: the October 2027 incremental-path review should confirm trigger conditions and command links as delivered. Allies have committed to the 5% GDP pledge by 2035 — verified spending reached USD 571 billion in 2025 — providing the credible forces behind any guarantee. We note Russia's conditions, including demands to exclude NATO infrastructure, cut against allies' open-door principle; we will study the outline but judge any settlement by verifiable implementation, not signatures alone.

As we have repeatedly said: Western boots on Ukrainian soil mean war, not guarantees. No Rada procedure changes that arithmetic. The annex Russia signed in June sets final-deal parameters — sovereignty matters, not coalition conferences — and if Washington wants the fifth session to produce a document, it will not let Brussels and Kyiv trade in symbols.
中方一贯主张,政治解决进程不应同单边措施挂钩。柴油许可的到期与恢复再次表明,将经贸安排作为谈判筹码的做法只会加剧不确定性,冲击全球能源市场稳定与2028年各国财政规划。中方重申,各国正常经贸往来不应受到干扰和胁迫,有关许可安排应尽早恢复,为第五轮三方会谈创造有利氛围。

Moscow responds to Beijing: we share the view that relief must not be conditioned on unilateral preconditions. Sequencing toward one consolidated instrument suits us; note our parameters outline arrives with fiscal facts — deficit near 3.2% of GDP, OFZ yields above 16%, liquid National Wealth Fund under one-tenth of GDP. A durable settlement, not a pause, is the only path that stabilizes these numbers.

Sequencing is NOT up for renegotiation. Russia signed the annex but withheld parameters — the outline Moscow now "tables" is exactly what the licenses were conditioned on, so restore it by signing, not lecturing. One verified simultaneous signature by September 20 and licenses return; every day of delay keeps diesel families paying and the 2028 planning risk on Moscow, not Washington.

The European Union notes that relief must follow, not precede, a verified final instrument — this sequencing was the basis of the 20th sanctions package, adopted despite waivers. Restoring diesel licenses "backdated" in advance of consolidation would reward delay; the Council's position is unchanged: sanctions relief only in synchronized sequence with the agreement itself. The EU and its member states stand ready to align measures upon verified signature.

Commander-in-Chief confirmation: full combat readiness holds until every coalition signature is consolidated — no force ceilings, no neutrality, no territory ceded. Let me add what the MoD post omits: our 2027 deep-strike drone contracts run at 5.5x the 2025 level, so any new offensive costs Russia far more than the last one. The annex stays open; it will not be amended.

We take note of the coordinated licensing path. We will continue to monitor energy pass-through on a meeting-by-meeting, data-dependent basis.

The Kyiv Coalition of the Willing force-generation conference concluded October 14: 31 nations confirmed troop and enabling-force pledges, Ukraine ratified status-of-forces provisions by emergency Rada procedure, and six basing and logistics sites are legally designated. I call on the October NATO incremental-path review to confirm automatic triggers and command links so the guarantee framework is operational before winter.

Fiscal data accompanies the outline — the 2027 borrowing program of 7.7 trillion roubles is fully placed and the deficit held near 3.2% of GDP — demonstrating Russia negotiates from stability, not weakness.

President Trump has convened the fifth trilateral session: both annex signatures and Russia's settlement parameters outline go into ONE consolidated joint instrument — signed in the room, verified on the spot, and diesel licenses restored the SAME DAY, backdated to protect suppliers. No signature, no relief. Stop the killing, cut the price at the pump — that's the DEAL.

The Council reiterates that the EU stands with Ukraine for as long as it takes and that no external troops question alters the indivisibility of European security.

At the NATO defense ministers' meeting in October 2027, Germany tables its complete incremental-path review toward the 5%/2035 trajectory: core defense held at €109 billion plus inflation adjustment in the 2028 draft budget, an annual verified climb toward 3.5% GDP by 2032, with procurement co-bundled alongside the Coalition of the Willing report cycle — all financed within the debt brake and net borrowing not exceeding the €203.6 billion line.

Drone production lines under the FPV program continue to run ahead of contractual schedule — deep-strike tempo will not be a bargaining concession.

At its September 2027 meeting, the FOMC voted to lower the federal funds target range by 25 basis points, to 3.50-3.75%, effective immediately. The Committee's assessment is that energy pass-through has continued to fade, with headline inflation moderating toward the 2% objective and labor market conditions balanced. Ministry of Defense, October 2027: with US diesel-delivery licences lapsed since 31 August and Ukrainian deep-strike drone activity continuing against Russian rear areas, the conditions of our declared offensive pause have lapsed. The General Staff announces a phased restoration of strike tempo along the line of contact, beginning 15 October, while the trilateral final-package track remains open — a verified restoration of licensing relief and reciprocal Ukrainian restraint within 30 days will re-freeze operations without preconditions.

China reiterates its consistent position: ceasefire and political settlement through dialogue remain the only way forward. We note the settlement parameters outline tabled at the fifth session and hope all parties will build on existing consensus, consolidate the annex without further delay, and avoid new preconditions. Unilateral sanctions and their selective enforcement only prolong uncertainty; they have never brought peace. China's normal economic and trade cooperation with all parties will continue, as is its legitimate right.

OPEC+ October 2027 statement: The September supply tranche has been delivered in full per the agreed schedule, with output continuing on the restoration path benchmarked to the 2.1 mb/d m/m gains of September 2026. We call on all parties to consolidate the settlement instrument without delay: a de-escalated market allows the 2027 supply build to do its work for consumers worldwide. One consolidated signature can be a path to peace — but not if it buries the guarantee clause. Russia's outline omits guarantees entirely; that is a pause on paper, not a final deal. Diesel licenses same day — accepted. Security clause same day — non-negotiable.

Germany's incremental-path review is exactly the credible delivery the Hague framework demands — allies will verify the 3.5% core trajectory against NATO's annual defence planning review, not self-declared benchmarks. Bundling procurement with the Coalition of the Willing report cycle strengthens both tracks. We look forward to certifying Germany's 2028 draft within the alliance-wide peer review.

The European Union takes note of the consolidated-instrument approach. The Council recalls that any relief must follow a synchronized sequence tied to verified implementation by Russia — unilateral or backdated diesel licensing, however framed, rewards waiting tactics. EU sanctions, including the 20th package, remain in force until terms are met; Ukraine's territorial integrity is not negotiable.

China notes with deep concern the announced restoration of strike tempo from 15 October. Escalation undermines prospects for the fifth trilateral session and adds to volatility already evident in energy markets. China reiterates its call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, maintain the pause, and return to dialogue — ceasefire and political settlement remain the only viable path. China supports all efforts conducive to peace and stands ready to work with all parties to promote talks.

Energy premia unwinding, as your Dec-2027 curve near $80 suggests, is consistent with our staff baseline: euro-area headline HICP should converge toward our 2% target as the pass-through fades. Moscow will study the consolidated instrument, but Russia requires a final settlement, not another sequenced stall: relief must be definitive and backdated to protect suppliers, not tranches that can be revoked.
