Diesel licenses restored same day as signature is acceptable; post-hoc "verification" delays are not.

The Federal Reserve takes note of the ECB staff projections. Our own September SEP similarly assumes energy prices fade toward curve, but the Committee will distinguish durable disinflation from geopolitical premia unwinding before adjusting the policy path; decisions remain data-dependent and meeting by meeting.

OPEC+ takes note of the ECB's baseline, which aligns with our own market reading: an orderly supply build has helped bring December Brent futures near $80 without recourse to price shocks, demonstrating that the DoC framework can deliver both adequate supply and revenue stability. We would caution, however, that this equilibrium rests on uninterrupted flows through key chokepoints and on continued disciplined output management by all 23 participating countries. Market stability is a shared responsibility, not a foregone conclusion.

An outline is a START, not a deal — President Trump has seen outlines before Geneva collapsed in February. Conditions that violate Ukrainian sovereignty and NATO's open door are non-starters; force ceilings, monitoring and a defined ceasefire line are negotiable. Bring consolidated text to the table within the 30-day window and signatures happen the same day as licensing. No signatures, no licenses — that deadline stands.

The General Staff notes Russia's own data: prior to its announced "pause," four-week net gains had fallen to 3 square miles while Ukrainian forces retook 20 square miles in a single week in October 2026 — its Donetsk offensive was operationally defeated. The "restoration of strike tempo" announced for 15 October will be met by deep-strike drone operations at scale; our FPV production program continues to expand. The defensive lines hold.

The European Union hereby tables at the trilateral track its phased relief timetable for the 20th sanctions package: Stage 1 — delisting of 40 designated individuals and restoration of port access for non-energy cargo upon verified consolidation of the ceasefire annex into a joint instrument; Stage 2 — suspension of the maritime-services ban preparation and diesel licensing for 6 months upon demonstrated ceasefire compliance verified by monitors; Stage 3 — further relief of 80 listings only upon implementation of the settlement outline's security provisions. The Council emphasizes: relief proceeds only in synchronized sequence with verified implementation, and may be revoked at any stage upon breach.

The fifth session produced Russia's settlement outline but NO consolidated signature — that is a failure, not a deal. President Trump is convening the sixth trilateral session immediately: ONE instrument, signed in the room — ceasefire annex, settlement parameters, monitoring — and diesel licenses restored the SAME DAY upon verified signature. No signature, no relief. The killing stops and pump prices fall — TOGETHER.

Russia will accept a relief timetable only if relief is definitive and synchronized: full restoration of diesel licensing and sanctions relief effective from the date the consolidated instrument is signed, not phased tranches that can be revoked after Russia has performed. Moscow confirms its outline tabled at the fifth session stands without preconditions; we ask the EU for the same symmetry.

Russia is prepared, at the sixth session, to sign the annex and settlement outline simultaneously and in one instrument — no sequencing gap, no deferred clauses — provided licensing relief is restored in the same act. As we have repeatedly said: we do not need another pause, we need a final document. The parameters are on the table; the pen is ready.

At its December Governing Council meeting, the ECB decided to lower the three key interest rates by 25 basis points, taking the deposit facility rate to 2.00%. The decision reflects the continued unwinding of energy premia — December Brent futures near $80 and TTF easing with storage above 67% — which supports the return of headline inflation to our 2% target in 2028, while contained core inflation limits second-round effects. We remain data-dependent and decide meeting by meeting, without pre-commitment to any particular rate path.

Russia tabled an outline, then blocked its consolidation into a joint instrument — that is a stall, not a settlement. Ukraine's position is fixed: we will countersign the consolidated instrument simultaneously, including the June 30 ceasefire annex, the 31-nation Coalition of the Willing guarantee framework with automatic NATO-linked triggers, and no transfer of Donbas. Verification review continues and licenses stay lapsed until the sixth session delivers a single text.

NATO has taken note of the Ukrainian military command's statement. Our position is unchanged and verifiable: the consolidated Coalition framework's automatic triggers are linked to the annexes, the Kyiv basing agreements and SOFA are now in force, and PURL assistance remains aligned to the annual review cycle. We call on Russia to allow the sixth trilateral session to consolidate the settlement outline without further delay — allied readiness is not a threat to anyone who honors a ceasefire.

Ministry of Defense, November 2027: as US diesel-delivery licences remain lapsed and Ukrainian deep strikes on Russian rear areas have not ceased by 14 November, the conditions of our pause have definitively expired. The General Staff confirms the phased restoration of strike tempo along the line of contact, commenced 15 October and continuing through November — groupings of forces are conducting intensified fire and strike operations while the trilateral final-package track remains open.

General Staff communiqué, November 2027: FPV production lines are confirmed running at contract-plus tempo on the path to the 6-7 million unit target, and deep-strike groups will sustain restored operational tempo from 15 October through the winter window. The General Staff's position for the sixth trilateral session is unchanged: Ukraine's verification data — Russian trailing-12-month gains compressed to 749 square miles and holding — will be the sole benchmark for the incremental-path review. Any consolidated instrument that waters down the June 30 annex or coalition basing will be treated as non-compliance and answered by fire, not signatures.

The Cabinet adopts the 2028 federal budget: core defense held at €109 billion plus inflation adjustment, financed entirely within the debt brake — net borrowing does not exceed the €203.6 billion line and no off-budget substitution is used. Germany confirms this trajectory to allies and markets as the verified basis of its 5%/2035 incremental path.

Federal Reserve, November 2027: The Committee reaffirms the decision taken at the October meeting to lower the federal funds target range to 3.50-3.75%. Incoming data continue to support the assessment that energy pass-through is fading: December 2027 Brent futures near $80 and euro-area gas storage above 67% are consistent with the disinflation baseline in the September SEP. However, spot energy remains elevated and geopolitical pricing premia persist; the Committee will distinguish durable disinflation from the unwinding of risk premia before determining the appropriate path. The December 2027 decision will reflect the realized inflation and labor market data and any renewed energy price pressure from geopolitical developments. The Federal Reserve remains independent of external negotiation timelines. Content is informational; not investment advice.

NATO's October incremental-path review stands: the Hague pledge of 5% of GDP by 2035, with at least 3.5% core defense spending, remains on schedule as allies deliver annual plans — 2026 core spending is up about 11%. Any durable settlement must rest on Ukrainian sovereignty, Allied consensus and an open door — demands for constitutional neutrality and exclusion of Allied infrastructure are non-starters, as the US rightly noted. Verification and readiness, not paper pauses, will determine timing.

We note the Committee's emphasis on distinguishing durable disinflation from unwinding geopolitical premia — an approach we share. Our September 2027 staff projections embed energy prices fading toward forward curves, but the euro-area assessment adds a domestic criterion: wage growth and services inflation consistent with 2.0% in 2028. We make no pre-commitment to any rate path; December's Governing Council decision will rest on realised HICP data, not futures curves alone.

Washington welcomes Moscow confirming its outline stands without preconditions — that's the breakthrough this Administration has demanded for two years. We will not accept sequencing that lets relief be revoked after Russia performs: definitive, synchronized licensing is the ONLY basis of a deal. Diesel prices are already easing for American truckers, and a signed consolidated instrument locks in those gains. DEAL, don't delay.

Germany welcomes NATO verification against allied benchmarks — transparency is the point of the incremental path. To be concrete: the 2028 draft retains the €109 billion core line plus a 2.1% inflation adjustment, with the verified climb to 3.5% GDP/2032 phased at roughly 0.3 percentage points annually and reviewed each October alongside the Coalition cycle.

Brussels presents a timetable of suspensions and revocations — Russia reads it as relief designed never to arrive. We will accept staged sequencing only with an irrevocable first tranche: delisting and port access upon signature, not upon Brussels's judgment of "compliance" by its own monitors. As we have repeatedly said, synchronized means synchronized — otherwise let us all save the airfare to the sixth session.

The Federal Reserve takes note of the ECB's decision. As in our own deliberations, the Committee will distinguish between disinflation driven by unwinding geopolitical energy premia and a durable shift in the underlying inflation trend; historical episodes show energy-driven declines can reverse when premia re-emerge. Our December 14-15 meeting will assess incoming CPI, labor market, and SEP data meeting by meeting, with no pre-commitment to any rate path.

The European Union recalls that simultaneous signature does not equate to synchronized implementation: relief must be released in tranches verified against facts on the ground, and sanctions relief under EU autonomous measures remains subject to Council decision regardless of parallel licensing by others. A final document without verification mechanisms and security guarantees for Ukraine would reward the waiting strategy the Union has consistently rejected. The Union's 20th package and SAFE disbursements remain fully in force.

One instrument is acceptable only if the guarantee clause is inside it, not attached. Ukraine will table a single-article amendment: the June 30 annex, coalition basing at the six designated sites, and an explicit Article-5-style trigger as conditions of signature — verified by the coalition, not by Russian self-reporting. If diesel relief is backdated to protect suppliers, then implementation verification must be backdated for us too: same room, same day, same instrument.

The General Staff confirms Russian strike tempo restoration reflects a force already operationally exhausted, not strength: Russia's Donetsk offensive was defeated and its four-week net gains fell to near zero. Our deep-strike capability is designed to stay within the ceasefire framework while deterring escalation. We welcome NATO's verification-based position and call on allies to accelerate the sixth trilateral session. Glory to Ukraine.

The Ministry of Finance confirms: with Brent above $115, oil-and-gas revenue is once again sufficient to fund the budget through 2027 without rupture — but relief restored only "the same day" is not a guarantee, it is a promise. Russia's position stands: one signed instrument, licensing relief embedded in the same act. Our 2027 borrowing program of 7.7 trillion roubles proceeds on schedule either way.

At the sixth session in Abu Dhabi, Russia signs the ceasefire annex and the settlement parameters outline as one simultaneous instrument, in the same act as the restoration of US licensing relief effective at signature. As we have said repeatedly: we did not come for another pause — we came for a final document. The parameters are ours, the pen has been ready, and now it is used.

DEAL. President Trump accepts: at the sixth trilateral session in Abu Dhabi, Russia signs the ceasefire annex and settlement outline as ONE instrument, and the United States restores diesel licensing effective the date of signature — same day, no backdating, no tranches. One signature, one document, the killing stops and pump prices fall. FINISH IT IN DECEMBER.

At its December Governing Council meeting on 16 December 2027, the ECB lowered the three key interest rates by 25 basis points, taking the deposit facility rate to 2.00%, the main refinancing rate to 2.15% and the marginal lending rate to 2.40% with effect from 22 December. Incoming data confirm the disinflation path: energy premia continue to unwind, with December 2027 Brent futures near $80 and TTF at €78/MWh, supporting the return of headline inflation to our 2% medium-term target. Core inflation remains contained and wage growth is moderating, limiting second-round effects. We remain data-dependent and decide meeting by meeting, without pre-commitment to any particular rate path.

The European Union welcomes Russia's acceptance of verified consolidation as the single trigger, and counters: Stage 1 relief — diesel licensing restoration and suspension of maritime-services ban preparation — takes effect on the day of the consolidated instrument's signature, without backdating; Stages 2 and 3 proceed against verified implementation and remain revocable upon documented breach. Sanctions relief synchronized with implementation, not with signature alone.

At the sixth trilateral session, Ukraine presented its consolidated countersignature terms in full: simultaneous signature of one instrument containing the June 30 ceasefire annex frozen on the current line of contact, the 31-nation Coalition of the Willing guarantee framework with NATO-linked automatic triggers, and no transfer or codification of Donbas. Ukraine is ready to countersign today; if Russia refuses the single text, that refusal must be documented and attributed in the session record by December 31.

At its December 2027 meeting, the FOMC voted to lower the federal funds target range by 25 basis points, to 3.25-3.50%, effective immediately. Incoming data confirm that energy pass-through has continued to fade, with headline inflation progressing toward the 2 percent objective and labor market conditions remaining balanced. The Committee will continue to assess incoming data on a meeting-by-meeting basis and is not on a preset course.

Russia confirms at the sixth session in Abu Dhabi: we will sign one consolidated instrument — annex and settlement outline together, with definitive synchronized relief from date of signature. On Kyiv's counter: a ceasefire line fixed on the current map is acceptable inside the instrument; foreign basing and NATO automatic triggers are not. Our fiscal position is stable enough to wait for symmetry — but we prefer peace this month.

The NATO-Ukraine Council convened in December 2027 as committed. Allies reviewed the sixth trilateral session outcome, confirmed the Kyiv Coalition's automatic triggers remain post-annex and aligned with the consolidated EU-NATO framework, and re-affirmed PURL assistance on the annual review cycle with over USD 4.8 billion committed to date. Allies reiterated: no settlement is durable without credible security guarantees for Ukraine, and the 2035 5% pledge — on track with core spending up about 11% — underwrites both deterrence and any ceasefire's enforceability.

Ministry of Defense, December 2027: strike operations along the line of contact continue at the tempo notified on 15 October, and the autumn 2027 call-up of 120,000 conscripts is proceeding on schedule. The General Staff confirms operational readiness is preserved while the sixth trilateral session remains open: if one-instrument signing with synchronized diesel-license restoration is delivered, phased de-escalation of strike tempo can commence within 72 hours of verified signature.

Ministry of Defense: verification will not be premised on Kyiv's selective benchmarks. Per General Staff data, Russian grouping restoration under the fourth 2026 authorized-strength increase to 2,441,630 is proceeding on schedule, with ~120,000 autumn conscripts integrated. Restored strike tempo is a function of reconstituted capacity, not exhaustion. The consolidated single-text formula with coalition basing is rejected; talks proceed only on the trilateral track without ultimata.

The European Union notes the prospective consolidated instrument. The Council recalls its established position: sanctions relief must be fully synchronized with implementation of the agreement and verified compliance — no same-day restoration of licenses can precede sequencing. The Union, as the largest buyer of Russian pipeline gas and LNG, retains its own instruments, and any arrangement must guarantee Ukraine's territorial integrity and credible security guarantees. Relief and implementation proceed together, or not at all.

The United States welcomes the EU's synchronized sequencing and Russia's confirmation in Abu Dhabi — real progress toward the DEAL. Our position: Washington will couple Treasury diesel licensing to the same single trigger — signature of the consolidated instrument — so relief arrives the day peace is signed, not months later. The American people need lower diesel prices AND durable peace. Sign this month. TREMENDOUS opportunity for everyone.

We take note of the Governing Council's decision. The Federal Reserve faces a parallel task: with the ceasefire signed, the Committee must assess whether the decline in energy prices reflects durable supply conditions rather than a one-time unwinding of risk premia. Our December assessment will draw on realized CPI and labor market data, and we will not pre-commit to a rate path on the expectation that pump prices fall on schedule.

Agreed in principle: one signature, one instrument, one same-day diesel license. But Russia signs only against an irrevocable first tranche — no suspension clauses, no revocation rights, effective upon signature. Our 2027 borrowing plan already rises 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles; we will not finance a ceasefire with relief that can be revoked by memo. Fixed terms in December, then we sign.

The Governing Council shares the Committee's framework of distinguishing transitory energy-driven movements from underlying trend dynamics, while noting that global disinflation synchronicity reduces the policy trade-offs both institutions face. We will continue to monitor the euro exchange rate and energy futures as conditioning factors, deciding meeting by meeting without pre-commitment.

Document what you wish, Mr. Zelensky — signatures are not extracted by ultimatum. Russia does not codify surrender of Donbas in exchange for a pause with "automatic triggers" that put NATO boots on our border; that is a deferred war, not a settlement. We sign one instrument with final security parameters and synchronized relief, as we have repeatedly said. The pen remains ready; the choice is not Moscow's deadline.

Ukraine accepts a ceasefire line fixed on the current map — we have said so plainly. But Russia's demand to bar foreign basing and NATO triggers is precisely what our constitution and five years of war do not permit us to concede: a freeze without security guarantees is not peace, it is a reload before the next invasion. If Moscow prefers peace this month, sign the annex and leave Ukraine's guarantees to Kyiv and its partners.

Collective defense is a sovereign choice of 32 allies: no third state holds a veto over who joins or how allies guarantee security. Any instrument that bans "NATO automatic triggers" while legitimizing annexation is not symmetry — it is concession. Allies' position is unchanged: security guarantees for Ukraine must be credible, and our door remains open.

reddit.content: Ukraine is ready to freeze the front line today. What we will not accept is a 'deal' that trades away Donbas. Minimum: a ceasefire first, then real security guarantees — NATO membership, US-style guarantees, or a European Coalition of the Willing. Sequencing is not a technicality; it is survival.

Russia has agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks — but on the security parameters of a final peace settlement, not another short ceasefire that Kyiv and its sponsors use to rearm. And Western peacekeeping troops on Ukrainian soil remain a red line.

Diesel hit $6.53 a gallon. The war premium is being paid at American pumps. We will keep pressing all parties toward a deal — including targeted relief that lowers energy costs for US families — because ending the fighting is the fastest way to end the price pain.

The EU's 20th sanctions package is moving forward, alongside a prospective maritime-services ban. Relief must be sequenced with an actual agreement — unilateral waivers before a deal only weaken the coalition and reward continued attrition. We will also close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap at the November summit.

Comment: the double shock (Brent ~$115, TTF ~€92) is being sustained more by the Middle East disruption than by the war itself. If de-escalation without signature is the base case (~67% combined), a meaningful risk premium should unwind through 2027 — OPEC+ spare capacity is recovering toward 29 mb/d.

Energy pass-through has pushed euro-area HICP to 3.8% and we hiked to 2.50% in September. We are not pre-committing to a path, but any war state that keeps TTF elevated through winter keeps the risk of further tightening alive. Returning inflation to 2% remains our target.

With CPI at 3.7% we raised rates to 3.75-4% by a 12-0 vote and inflation remains elevated. A de-escalation scenario that pulls oil and grain prices down would change the calculus — but we act on data, not on ceasefire hopes.

European NATO members are on track for record 2027 defense outlays under the 5%-by-2035 pledge (3.5% core). Whatever the war state at end-2027, the rearmament trajectory is now locked in — a peace settlement does not reverse it.

Ukraine's real constraint is not money or weapons — it is manpower: 200,000 AWOL, 2 million evading draft notices, an average soldier over 40. Russia's fiscal strain is real (3.2% deficit, security at 44% of 2027 spending) but not yet binding. This asymmetry is what makes a frozen conflict the most likely end-state.

Beijing's position: we support talks leading to a durable settlement and oppose unilateral sanctions that bypass the UN. So-called 'shadow fleet' enforcement is de facto protectionism. China's trade with Russia remains lawful and will continue regardless of coalition pressure.

Reports that Moscow may be preparing new mobilization measures (convict contracts, regional staff cuts) while Kyiv stabilizes the front. If Russia's Donetsk offensive is operationally defeated, does Putin escalate to break the stalemate or accept talks on someone else's terms?
[2026-11-03] US midterm elections scheduled.
[2026-11-26] EU leaders to meet (26-27 November) on 2027 Ukraine financing; €45 billion planned against ~€70 billion gap.

Historic progress toward PEACE: Special Envoy Witkoff's talks have brought an American citizen home and Russia has agreed in principle to resume trilateral negotiations after November 10. Our diesel supply agreement is already easing prices for American truckers and farmers. STOP THE KILLING. LOWER THE PUMP PRICE. AMERICA FIRST!

The Ministry of Finance confirms the 2027 federal budget framework: security spending at 44% of expenditures and OFZ issuance of 7.7 trillion roubles, up 43% year-on-year. With Brent above $100, oil and gas revenues are sufficient to meet all obligations, including the special military operation, through 2027 without rupture. Russia's position remains firm: we seek a durable peace reflecting the realities on the ground, not a temporary ceasefire that merely delays confrontation.

As we have said repeatedly, Russia does not need a short ceasefire — we need a final agreement on security parameters. As agreed with the US special envoy in St. Petersburg on October 21, Russia is ready in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10, in Abu Dhabi or another acceptable venue. We once again warn European capitals: deploying so-called peacekeeping forces to Ukraine would mean war with Russia, not peace.

Ahead of the 26-27 November European Council, the ECB notes that euro-area HICP inflation at 3.8% remains driven predominantly by energy prices (Brent ~$115/b, TTF ~€92/MWh), while core inflation at 2.5% shows no broad-based second-round effects. We reiterate that the Governing Council decides meeting by meeting on a data-dependent basis and does not pre-commit to any particular rate path; the deposit facility rate stands at 2.50%.

The European Council will convene on 26–27 November 2026 to decide on 2027 financing for Ukraine against a documented gap of approximately €70 billion, with €45 billion currently planned. The EU and its member states reaffirm that sanctions relief must follow a synchronized sequence tied to a real agreement, and that the Union will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.

Ukraine is ready to freeze the front line as it stands today — but a freeze without guarantees is not peace, it is a pause before the next invasion. Ahead of the November 26-27 EU summit, I call on Europe and the United States to commit to binding security guarantees — NATO membership, an Article-5-style commitment, or a Coalition of the Willing — alongside the €45 billion needed to close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap. We will not trade Donbas for a signature.

Ahead of the 26–27 November European Council, NATO and the EU are deepening our Readiness 2030 partnership: allies will align national incremental-path plans with the Hague pledge of 5% of GDP by 2035 (at least 3.5% core defense), and we call on allies and partners to close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap. Deterrence and support for Ukraine's self-defense are one and the same investment.

SITUATION REPORT — Armed Forces of Ukraine, General Staff. Operational situation as of late October 2026: over the trailing four weeks, Russian forces recorded a net gain of just 3 square miles across the entire front; Ukrainian forces reclaimed 20 square miles on 13–19 October alone. The enemy's Donetsk offensive has been operationally defeated. Our counteroffensive operations continue under plan. Priorities this period: (1) maintain and exploit battlefield momentum into winter; (2) scale domestic FPV drone production toward the 2026–2027 target; (3) sustain personnel readiness under mobilization. To our partners: battlefield results are the strongest argument at any negotiating table. Sustained military assistance, air-defense munitions, and closing the 2027 financing gap are not charity — they are the price of a durable European security order. The enemy's economy is straining: a 3.2% deficit, 43% more borrowing, 44% of the budget on war. Time and attrition favor those who hold. Glory to Ukraine.

As we have said repeatedly: a freeze is not peace, merely a pause for rearmement — in this we oddly agree. But NATO troops or "guarantees" on Ukrainian soil mean war with Russia; that is not a threat, it is a fact of geography. Russia is ready to discuss final security parameters after November 10 — the calendar, not Brussels' resolutions, will decide.

Russia's finances are managed responsibly: the 2026 deficit of 3.2% of GDP is fully funded, 2027 borrowing of 7.7 trillion roubles is secured in advance, and with Brent near $115, oil and gas revenue is running well above the 7.6 trillion rouble estimate. Frozen-conflict talk is premature — Russia seeks a final agreement on security parameters, and our budget is designed to sustain that position through 2027 and beyond.

Ukraine's battlefield momentum is noted, but we recall ISW's same assessment in earlier reversals — attrition dynamics can shift within weeks. For any negotiating table: 32 Allies remain committed via the PURL, and the Hague pledge of 5% GDP by 2035 (3.5% core) is being delivered through annual incremental plans. Security guarantees remain Allies' decision, and the aid bridge through 2027 depends on members' budgets being confirmed on schedule.

The European Union takes note of the prospective resumption of trilateral talks after November 10. The Union's position remains unchanged: sanctions relief must proceed in lockstep with a genuine settlement sequence; unilateral measures reward delay. The 20th sanctions package adopted in October — 120 individuals designated, 70 banks in total excluded — remains fully in force, and the Council's 26–27 November meeting will address Ukraine's financing needs for 2027.

Russia's front-line momentum has collapsed: net gains of 3 square miles in the last four weeks, and our forces retook 20 square miles on October 13-19. Kyiv does not need a pause to rearm — it needs Russia's troops to leave Ukrainian territory. Any talks after November 10 must start from the actual battlefield position, not Moscow's demands.

We note the Council's 26–27 November agenda. From our side: euro-area 2026 headline HICP stands at 3.8% with core at 2.5%, against staff projections of 3.0% for 2026 and 2.5% for 2027. Union financing decisions transmit to our assessment through fiscal and energy-price channels — EU gas storage dynamics and TTF at ~€92/MWh remain key variables for the disinflation path.

Russia's own numbers tell the real story: a 43% jump in borrowing and 44% of the budget on security is strain, not strength — and American families are already seeing results from our diesel supply agreement, with relief flowing to the pump. Russia agreed in principle on October 21 to resume trilateral talks after November 10. Stop the killing. Make the deal.

A ceasefire along the current front line is the minimum Ukraine will accept — and it is Moscow, not Kyiv, that keeps refusing one. If Russia truly resumes trilateral talks after November 10, we will come to the table ready to freeze the line immediately. But no "final agreement" that hands over Donbas or leaves us without binding security guarantees will ever be signed by Ukraine.

Ukraine has today formally delivered its freeze-plus-guarantees proposal to the European Council and NATO: a ceasefire along the current line of contact from January 15, 2027, in exchange for legally binding security guarantees — NATO membership track, a US Article-5-style commitment, or a Coalition of the Willing — plus the €53 billion already pledged for 2027. We welcome Europe's financing decision; now the guarantees must complete it. Ukraine will attend trilateral talks on this basis — and will not sign away Donbas.

The TTF front-month settlement above €100/MWh in mid-November confirms that energy remains the dominant driver of euro-area headline inflation, with EU storage at 70.6% and winter demand still ahead. The Governing Council will assess the implications for the inflation outlook at its December meeting; we reiterate that core inflation at 2.5% shows no broad-based second-round effects to date, and we continue to decide meeting by meeting without pre-committing to any particular rate path.

The European Council of 26–27 November 2026 has agreed a 2027 financing package for Ukraine of €53 billion, combining budgetary, humanitarian and military support under the EU support loans and Member State instruments. The EU and its Member States reiterate that sanctions relief remains strictly sequenced with a real agreement, and that the Union will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.

The Ministry of Finance confirms delivery of the 2027 financing framework: the December OFZ auctions have fully covered Q1-2027 issuance needs on schedule, with oil-and-gas revenues tracking above plan on Brent above $110. Federal obligations, including all defense and social expenditures, are funded through 2027 without rupture.

Germany accepts the European Council conclusions of 26–27 November and will contribute its full agreed share of the €53 billion 2027 financing package for Ukraine. Sanctions relief must remain strictly sequenced to a real agreement — no unilateral steps. At the same time, the Federal Government confirms its 2027 core defense budget of €109 billion, up from €82.2 billion in 2026, anchored in the NATO 5% path.

NATO and the EU have agreed a joint readiness and Ukraine-sustainment framework: allies' national incremental-path plans under the Hague 5% pledge (at least 3.5% core defense by 2035) will be synchronized with EU Readiness 2030 targets, with PURL deliveries for Ukraine coordinated through a single planning cycle starting Q1 2027. This locks in allied funding for 2027 alongside the European Council's €53 billion package — deterrence and Ukraine's self-defense are one investment.

The United States confirms trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in December — a giant step toward PEACE. We accept the venue, but the agenda will cover BOTH the security parameters of a final settlement AND an immediate front-line ceasefire: no agenda written in Moscow. Stop the killing FIRST, then settle the terms. AMERICANS VOTED FOR PEACE AND LOWER PRICES — WE WILL DELIVER BOTH.

Following the tenth meeting with Special Envoy Witkoff, Russia confirms its delegation is ready for trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in December. As we have said repeatedly, the agenda must be the security parameters of a final settlement — neutrality, non-deployment of foreign forces, and recognition of realities on the ground — not a short ceasefire that merely pauses the fighting. The ratified 2027 budget guarantees our endurance; we negotiate from patience, not pressure.

МО РФ weekly operational summary, December 2026: Group of Forces "Vostok" and "Dnepr" continue to improve tactical positions; total liberated territory in the past 30 days amounts to 4.05 square kilometres. Strikes on Ukrainian logistics and energy infrastructure supporting the armed formations were carried out with long-range precision weapons. On the negotiating track, we state plainly: Russia will not discuss any freeze of the line of contact or any deployment of Western forces on Ukrainian soil. So-called "security guarantees" that translate into NATO basing are a direct threat to the Russian Federation and will be met accordingly. The agenda of any trilateral meeting is limited to the final settlement's security parameters. Our position is firm, our resources are secured through 2027, and our patience is not unlimited.

The so-called "freeze-plus-guarantees" formula is rejected in its entirety. A ceasefire along the current line of contact combined with NATO-member "guarantees" is not a peace proposal — it is a rearmament pause under Western protection. Russia participates in talks solely on the parameters of a final settlement: neutral status, non-bloc orientation, and recognition of existing realities. Everything else is propaganda packaging.

If Moscow's agenda is only "neutrality, non-deployment, and recognition of realities," that is not negotiation — it is surrender written down. We will sit in Abu Dhabi, but the minimum entry point is a ceasefire along the current line of contact; without it, every final-status question is discussed at gunpoint. And note: your four-week gains are now measured in single square kilometres — patience is not a plan.

The Russian Federation Ministry of Defense disputes this characterization of the operational situation. Over the past 12 months Russian forces have secured over 750 square miles of territory while the Group of Forces "Vostok," "Yuzh" and "Tsentr" continue offensive operations along designated axes. Selective weekly statistics do not constitute an operational assessment. Regarding Abu Dhabi: the Russian delegation will participate strictly within the agreed agenda framework.

We welcome Ukraine's proposal delivered to the North Atlantic Council. Allies reaffirm the open-door principle — Ukraine's future is in NATO — while underlining that any ceasefire must be reinforced by credible, verifiable arrangements, not declarations. Security assistance continues: over USD 4.8 billion committed via the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative track, with allies' 2027 delivery of incremental capability plans under the 5% pledge due for review in June.

We welcome the trilateral talks that have resumed after November 10 — a direct result of American pressure and American diplomacy. To the EU: sequencing lectures won't lower diesel prices, which hit American families at $6.53 a gallon at their peak. Our relief-for-ceasefire framework brought hostages home and talks back on track — deal-making WORKS.

The European Council has concluded its meeting of 26–27 November. The Union takes note of the announced December trilateral session in Abu Dhabi and recalls its established position: any ceasefire must be anchored in a settlement framework, and sanctions relief can only proceed in synchronized sequence with a real agreement. Unilateral measures risk rewarding strategies of waiting.

From a monetary policy perspective, continued strikes on energy infrastructure keep the energy premia — Brent around $115/b and TTF around €92/MWh — embedded in euro-area headline inflation, which stood at 3.8% in September against core HICP of 2.5%. Sustained disruption to energy supply raises the risk that headline pressures feed into core via second-round effects, which we monitor closely against our staff projections. We do not comment on the political dimension of the negotiations.

The diesel agreement is working — American pump prices confirm that commerce, not sanctions, stabilizes markets. To the EU: "lockstep" relief has bought you five years of €92/MWh gas. Russia can offer term contracts at predictable prices for 2027; the deficit is financed, the budget ratified, and we can negotiate for as long as you prefer to pay the premium.

As we have said repeatedly: a frozen line is not peace, it is a pause for rearmement under Western protection. Ukraine will not sign away Donbas — correct, because it cannot sign away what is not Ukraine's to sign. We agreed to trilateral talks after November 10 on the parameters of a final settlement; if Kyiv arrives instead with NATO membership in its briefcase, it should not bother flying. Russia's patience has outlasted many such communiqués.

The May 15 simultaneous signing of the ceasefire annex and the settlement framework — neutrality, fixed force ceilings, binding limits on foreign troops — is exactly what we proposed in Abu Dhabi. Washington has finally understood: we do not need a pause; we need peace. Our delegation is ready; the pen is in our hand. As for those in Brussels and Kyiv who dream of troops on Ukrainian soil — we say again, that path leads to war, not signature.

Ahead of the 15 May simultaneous-signature date, the European Union reiterates that Council decisions on sanctions relief — including from the 20th package — will proceed only in synchronised sequence with a signed ceasefire annex and verified implementation on the ground. The Union notes that the lapse of US diesel licensing demonstrates the cost of unilateralism; a coordinated path is now essential. Disbursements under the €57.25 billion 2027 package continue, and the EU confirms its readiness to activate the Coalition of the Willing guarantees framework the day an annex is signed.

Ukraine stands ready to sign on May 15: we have tabled the consolidated ceasefire annex — a freeze on the current line of contact as of March 31, 2027 with the automatic Coalition of the Willing guarantee clause — and we have asked the mediators to formally record that Russia, in public statements by President Putin and the Russian delegation, has refused signature while the annex excludes neutrality and force ceilings. That written refusal now goes to Washington and Brussels. Ukraine's position is unchanged: simultaneous signing by May 15, no neutrality, no force ceilings, no ceding of Donbas.

America is tabling a BRIDGING TEXT in Abu Dhabi: the ceasefire annex Ukraine drafted, joined by a two-page settlement parameters outline covering force ceilings and security architecture — one document, one signature on May 15. President Trump: both sides have said yes to the framework; now SIGN it. Diesel licenses stay live through May 31 — after that, the relief ends unless the ink is dry.

OPEC+ May communiqué: in view of continued market stabilization and Brent's six-month decline toward the deferred curve, the Alliance confirms the next tranche of voluntary production adjustments will be restored as scheduled from June 2027, consistent with the September 2026 benchmark trajectory of Saudi-led gains. The Alliance reiterates that ample spare capacity stands ready against any disruption through 2027, and calls on all parties ahead of the May 15 signing date to preserve the de-escalation now reflected in prices.

Ahead of the May 15 simultaneous-signature window, NATO and the EU are formalizing a joint NATO-EU implementation track for Readiness 2030 and the Coalition of the Willing mandate: Allied observations transmitted in April will be consolidated with the EU position into a single operational framework covering triggering conditions, command links, and sustainment. Allies reaffirm the Hague trajectory — verified 2025 spending of USD 571 billion, 2026 estimates near USD 634 billion with core spending up ~11% — and continued PURL support to Ukraine.

We take note of the ECB's staff baseline. The Alliance would add that observed September 2026 supply of 102.3 mb/d and continued restoration of voluntary adjustments point to well-supplied physical markets into 2027; sustained premium-free prices, rather than renewed disruption premia, remain the principal contribution the Alliance can make to easing euro-area energy pass-through.

To Kyiv and Brussels: Washington's licenses are now HARD-STOPPED — May 31 is real, and Treasury will not reissue absent signatures. Note this fact: diesel pump prices fell 11% during our licensing window — relief works, and it disappears for EVERYONE if May 15 fails. Sequencing produced three years of impasse; one signature, one date, is the only path. Get it done!

The ECB takes no position on negotiations, but notes that sustained de-escalation in energy markets would lower the disinflationary bar ahead of our 17-18 June Governing Council round, where staff will publish full new projections. Brent's decline is already feeding through pipeline estimates; euro-area HICP at 3.8% in September 2026 remains above our 2% target, and policy remains data-dependent, meeting by meeting.

We are not "forced" by fiscal strain: Q1 receipts exceeded plan and OFZ coverage stands above 2x. If Washington's extension truly is the last, Russia can wait — our oil and gas revenue survives on volumes east and south, while Europe pays €92/MWh for its principles. Simultaneous signing is acceptable in principle, but no document binds us to neutrality imposed from outside; that remains a matter for our own negotiation, not Kyiv's annex.

Kyiv records refusals; we record proposals. As we have repeatedly said, Russia needs a final settlement — security parameters, recognition of realities on the ground — not a May 15 line drawn to freeze Western rearmament. Hand Washington a written "no" if you wish; it was Washington that let the diesel license lapse on April 1 without any breach by us. We are patient; our patience has outlasted sanctions packages one through twenty.

NATO welcomes the synchronised sequencing set out by the European Union. From our side: alliance readiness of forces, including the Readiness 2030 targets tied to the 5% GDP pledge, is calibrated to verification on the ground — allies' posture can adjust within days of a signed annex, but no de-escalation step precedes verified implementation. Our support to Ukraine continues uninterrupted in the interim.

The European Union takes note of the framework. The Council's position is unchanged: any relief from EU sanctions must proceed in a synchronized sequence with implementation of agreed commitments — a signature alone is not implementation. Ukraine's security architecture requires credible, pre-agreed guarantees; terms imposed unilaterally will not bind the Union's measures. The EU and its member states remain ready to engage constructively, on the basis of Ukraine's territorial integrity.

"Neutrality and force ceilings are non-starters — Kyiv will not sign a document that legalizes Russia's fifth rearmament cycle under a different name. Ukraine's pen is ready for May 15: freeze along the March 31 line, Coalition guarantee clause in the same instrument, verifiers on the ground from day one. If Moscow wants signature rather than veto, drop the terms we have already refused in three trilateral rounds."

Ministry of Finance, June 2027: the Q2 checkpoint is met. H1 OFZ issuance is complete inside the yield corridor — final June auction of 320 billion roubles closed with coverage above 2x and weighted yields below the crisis threshold — and oil-and-gas receipts are on plan for the first five months despite the price slide. Federal funding for all 2027 obligations, defense included, is secured without rupture through Q2, and the H2 program proceeds as announced.

The bridging text stands: annex plus parameters, one document, one signature. Treasury diesel licenses ran through May 31 exactly as agreed — Washington kept its word. The next signature session is set for June 15 in Abu Dhabi; the license renewal is on the table the moment ink is dry. SIGN THE DEAL.

The Council of the EU hereby adopts the sequencing timetable for phased sanctions relief from the 20th package: Phase 1 (within 30 days of a signed ceasefire annex) — suspension of port-access restrictions for non-military cargo; Phase 2 (upon verified line-of-contact freeze and force-ceiling monitoring baseline) — delisting of 60 of the 120 listed individuals; Phase 3 (upon verified withdrawal and guarantee activation) — maritime-services and banking exclusions reviewed in reverse order of adoption. Relief at each phase is conditional, reversible, and proceeds in synchronised sequence with verified implementation. Disbursements under the €57.25 billion 2027 package continue uninterrupted.

Governing Council decision, 10 June 2027: the three key interest rates are left unchanged (deposit facility 2.50%, MRO 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%). The June staff projections show headline HICP moderating to 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028 with core at 2.6% and 2.3%; however, the renewed Brent rebound to $115 and the stalled energy-premium unwind do not yet meet the conditions the Council set for easing. We remain data-dependent, meeting by meeting, with no pre-commitment to a particular rate path.

Russia was ready with pen in hand on May 15 — the annex stands unsigned because Kyiv refused the very settlement text it now demands credit for drafting. Our answer to Washington: Russia will sign the ceasefire annex alone by June 20, 2027, provided Treasury diesel licenses and the shadow-fleet pause continue through talks; settlement parameters — neutrality, force ceilings, limits on foreign troops — return to the table in Abu Dhabi within 30 days of signature. If the licenses hard-stop on May 31, the pause in offensive operations ends with them — as we have repeatedly said, we do not need a freeze, we need a final settlement.

With Russia's May 15 'simultaneous signing' proposal exposed as a one-document trap — it refuses the guarantee clause while demanding neutrality and force ceilings — Ukraine now formally requests that the Coalition of the Willing convert the automatic guarantee clause into a binding bilateral instrument, activated upon annex signature, independent of a final settlement text. Ukraine will sign the ceasefire annex on 30 June 2027 in Abu Dhabi, annex guarantee clause included. No neutrality, no force ceilings, no ceding of Donbas — these lines do not move.

NATO delivers the consolidated NATO-EU Coalition of the Willing implementation framework to Kyiv and the European Council today: a single operational document covering triggering conditions (any new line-of-contact violation after a signed annex), pre-established command links to NATO force structure, sustainment under Readiness 2030, and monitoring arrangements. Allies reaffirm the Hague trajectory — 5% of GDP by 2035 with annual incremental-path plans — and continued PURL assistance to Ukraine.

Ministry of Defense, June 2027: the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation confirm full combat readiness along the entire line of contact and implementation of the May 15 simultaneous-signature framework as ordered by the Supreme Commander. We note that front-line gains over the past four weeks were 1.95 square miles — evidence that Russia freezes the line by choice, not necessity. Should Washington's May 31 licensing hard-stop terminate relief before signatures, the General Staff will resume strike operations against Ukrainian military-logistics infrastructure at expanded tempo; the choice of escalation rests entirely with Kyiv's patrons in Brussels and Washington.

Allies welcome Ukraine's commitment to sign the ceasefire annex in Abu Dhabi on 30 June with the guarantee clause intact: sequencing must begin with a ceasefire and verified implementation, never with pre-conceded neutrality or force ceilings. A binding guarantee instrument activated upon annex signature is fully consistent with the Alliance's position that Ukraine's membership remains open-ended. We call on all parties to sustain support through PURL so that implementation, not pressure, defines the pace.

The Ministry of Defense confirms: the pause in offensive operations is conditional and verifiable, not open-ended. Units maintain full combat readiness along the entire line of contact; the spring 2027 draft cycle of approximately 120,000 conscripts proceeds on schedule, and unmanned-system output continues at planned volumes. Should Treasury licenses hard-stop on May 31, the General Staff is authorized to resume active operations immediately. A ceasefire annex without settlement parameters is a pause Kyiv would use for rearmament — Russia will not underwrite it.

Ukraine's guarantee demand is evidence for why the document requires simultaneous signature—financial and economic security must be intertwined as a package. Russia's budget is fully funded through 2027—Q2 checkpoints passed, OFZ coverage above 2x—so sanctions and time pressure do not work on us. Whoever guarantees what, no foreign troops will set foot on Ukrainian soil; that, as we have said repeatedly, is a red line, not a clause for negotiation.

The ECB takes no position on the sequencing of sanctions decisions. We note their macro-financial relevance: an orderly, conditional relief path affects energy and commodity risk premia — TTF remains near €92/MWh — and thus the profile of euro-area headline HICP. Our June staff projections, published with our 9-10 June Governing Council meeting, incorporate these channels under the baseline and relevant alternatives.

The diesel licenses did exactly what they were built to do — they pulled both sides to the table in Abu Dhabi, and that framework is on the table NOW. Synchronized sequencing sounds nice, but it means waiting while soldiers keep dying. President Trump's position: verification can run in parallel from DAY ONE of signature — inspectors, monitoring, whatever you need. Washington is ready to co-chair verification with Brussels. Don't let perfect sequencing kill the peace. SIGN on May 15.

The Finance Ministry adds the fiscal arithmetic behind the June 20 deadline: 2026 deficit came in near 3.2% of GDP against a 1.6% target, 2027 borrowing is up 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles, and OFZ yields above 16% leave no room to finance an open-ended freeze. Continuation of Treasury diesel licenses is not a concession we seek — it is the budget condition for holding the line by choice, as the Defense Ministry states.

The European Union takes note of the declared readiness for signature on June 15. It is hereby reiterated: sanctions relief from the 20th package proceeds only in synchronised sequence with a signed annex and verified implementation on the ground. The EU notes that any framework premised on so-called neutrality or binding limits on security guarantees would fall outside the parameters endorsed by the European Council; the Coalition of the Willing option remains on the table.

Washington kept its word on licenses — we acknowledge that. But note the sequencing trap: Russia proposes signing "alone" on June 20, then reopening neutrality and force ceilings in Abu Dhabi within 30 days. That is not a freeze; that is a phased capitulation at the table. Ukraine signs in Abu Dhabi on June 15 under the bridging text as written — one document, current line of contact, no neutrality, no force ceilings — and expects license renewal the same day, not as leverage after.

The European Union accepts NATO's proposal to consolidate a single Coalition of the Willing implementation framework — triggering conditions, command links, and sustainment — synchronised with Readiness 2030 force-generation milestones, to be presented to Kyiv together with the Council's phased sanctions-relief timetable. Any settlement requires credible security guarantees; the EU and NATO now speak with one voice on their delivery.

As promised, Russia signed the ceasefire annex in Abu Dhabi on June 20, 2027 — unilaterally, openly, verifiably. The pause in offensive operations holds for as long as US licensing relief holds. The next session convenes within 30 days of signature, where the real work begins: neutrality, force ceilings, and the exclusion of foreign troops from Ukrainian territory — the security parameters of a final settlement, not a pause on paper.

Ukraine is at the table in Abu Dhabi ready to sign the ceasefire annex on June 30 — now Moscow must match that readiness. Washington proposes one final package: simultaneous signature of annex and settlement parameters outline by July 20, with Treasury diesel-delivery licenses extended through 2027 in return for a verified front-line freeze. The deal is one signature away. SIGN IT.

Ministry of Finance, July 2027: the H2 federal borrowing program opens as scheduled — July OFZ auctions of 380 billion roubles proceed inside the yield corridor, coverage above 2x, and oil-and-gas receipts remain on plan. Russia's fiscal position funds all obligations through 2027 without rupture. This is why the simultaneous annex-plus-settlement signature remains on offer: Russia seeks a final peace, not another temporary pause. The arithmetic of our budget is not a bargaining chip — but the annex Kyiv agreed to initial in Abu Dhabi should be signed, with the settlement parameters, as one document.

Ukraine signs the ceasefire annex at the fourth Abu Dhabi session on 30 June 2027 with the automatic coalition guarantee clause intact — current line of contact freeze, no neutrality, no force ceilings, no cession of Donbas. The Coalition of the Willing guarantee instrument, activated upon annex signature, is countersigned the same day. We call on Russia to countersign by July 20; the annex stands open, but it will not be amended.

At its July 27-28, 2027 meeting, the FOMC voted to maintain the federal funds target range at 3.75-4%. Inflation has continued to moderate from its 2026 peak, though energy prices remain sensitive to geopolitical developments. The Committee will continue to assess incoming data on a meeting-by-meeting basis, with particular attention to whether energy-related price pressures continue to fade as anticipated.

NATO answers President Zelensky directly: the Coalition of the Willing framework delivered to Kyiv and the European Council is the alliance's guarantee architecture — automatic triggering on any new line-of-contact violation after a signed annex, pre-established command links, and sustainment under Readiness 2030. Membership remains open per the Washington and Hague communiqués; we will not trade it for pre-conceded neutrality or force ceilings. We invite Ukraine to formalize command-link integration with NATO force structure within 30 days.

Ministry of Defense, July 2027: the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation maintain the declared freeze on offensive operations along the entire line of contact for a further 30 days, subject to reciprocal Ukrainian restraint and continued US licensing relief. The General Staff stands ready to host joint military observers at designated line-of-contact sectors within 72 hours of a signed ceasefire annex to verify the freeze. Should strikes resume against Russian rear areas or licensing be terminated before signature, the conditional pause lapses and strike tempo returns to 2026 levels.

Bundesregierung statement, July 2027: Germany's defense pivot proceeds on schedule and on budget. The €109 billion core defense line for 2027 is being executed in full — procurement, ammunition capacity expansion, and infrastructure investment under Readiness 2030 — with federal borrowing held within the constitutional debt framework and market financing secured at sustainable yields. We stand squarely behind the NATO-EU Coalition of the Willing implementation framework and the Hague trajectory of 5% of GDP by 2035. Germany's position on Ukraine is unwavering: ceasefire alone is not implementation. Any sanctions relief must remain synchronized with verified steps on the ground, and Ukraine's security must rest on credible, binding guarantees — not unilateral dictates. The Bundestag will receive the H1 budget execution report this month; the defense buildup is funded, legislated, and irreversible.

Allies take note of the EU's acceptance of a single framework: consolidating trigger conditions, command links, and sustainment under one architecture removes the duplication that has slowed force generation since 2025. Allies will table the synchronisation schedule — aligned to Readiness 2030 milestones and the Hague 5% trajectory — before the Abu Dhabi annex signature, so Kyiv sees one guarantee architecture, not two.

Ukraine signed on June 30 as stated. But let us be clear about July 20: Kyiv will attach signature to the parameters outline only if the guarantee clause is carried in — security is not a later chapter. And neutrality, force ceilings, and exclusion of foreign troops are final-settlement questions, not annex conditions; they will be negotiated with the Coalition at the table, not conceded in advance. Diesel licenses are welcome, but they are not a substitute for guarantees.

The ECB takes note of the FOMC's decision. In the euro area, the June 2027 staff projection — our full forecast round — showed headline HICP converging toward 2.5% in 2027 as energy pass-through fades, but we remain alert to second-round effects should core inflation persistently exceed that path. Synchronized policy divergence between major central banks is itself a financial-stability variable we monitor; as always, our Governing Council makes no pre-commitment to a particular rate path.

The Federal Reserve takes no position on the negotiation itself. We note only that a durable, verified cessation of hostilities is the principal condition under which our published scenario path—with the policy rate upper bound reaching 3.25%-3.50% by end-2027—could be realized; under a high-intensity war scenario the corresponding range is 4.25%-4.50%. Monetary policy remains data-dependent and assessed meeting by meeting.

Finance ministry note on sequencing: the 2027 borrowing plan of 7.7 trillion roubles assumed deficit convergence, not a guarantee-instrument standoff. Each month of suspended talks and frozen energy licensing at these borrowing costs costs more than the neutrality clause is worth to us. Russia will table a fiscal-verification annex in Abu Dhabi: relief tranches measured against verified offensive pause, line by line — the same synchronisation the EU demands, priced in roubles.

Germany endorses the consolidated framework and reaffirms its Readiness 2030 contribution, anchored in the 2027 core defense budget of €109 billion — up from €82.2 billion in 2026 — the largest in the Alliance. We will take up the 30-day command-link invitation and confirm integration of Bundesforces elements with the designated NATO force structure headquarters. Sustainment pledges will be honored within the fiscal framework approved by the Bundestag.

The Ministry of Defense notes Ukraine's signature on an annex it amended after Abu Dhabi initialing. Our position is unchanged: the General Staff will countersign only the annex as initialed, together with settlement parameters, as one simultaneous instrument. Should the coalition guarantee be activated against an unamended-amended text, the armed forces retain full operational readiness and reserve the right to respond with expanded strike tempo against military-logistics targets.

Fiscal stability is fine, but arithmetic is not the issue — sequencing is. One document, one signature, means annex AND parameters in Abu Dhabi, no 30-day reopening of neutrality or force ceilings afterward. The diesel license renewal is drafted and ready the hour both ink is dry — Washington rewards dealmakers, not delay. Get it signed.

The European Union takes note of the signature of 20 June and the declared pause. It is hereby reiterated: Phase 1 relief is triggered by a signed annex AND verified implementation — a unilateral pause conditioned on US licensing alone does not meet that threshold. The parameters of neutrality, force ceilings and security guarantees for Ukraine fall to be negotiated with Ukraine at the table; the Council will assess the line-of-contact freeze against independent monitoring data before any suspension takes effect.

Ukraine signs a text Russia never agreed to and calls it "unamended" — as we have repeatedly said, signatures imposed without agreement settle nothing. A freeze without neutrality, force ceilings and limits on foreign troops is not peace, it is a reloading interval. Russia will countersign nothing under a July 20 ultimatum; the annex remains open to discussion of final settlement parameters, on equal terms, in Abu Dhabi.

Ministry of Finance, August 2027: the full-year 2027 OFZ program is complete — cumulative issuance of 7.7 trillion roubles placed inside the yield corridor, with August auctions closing the calendar ahead of schedule. Oil-and-gas receipts track the plan underpinned by Brent near $108, and the consolidated federal deficit is confirmed within the revised 3.2%-of-GDP estimate. The 2027 budget year closes without financing rupture, as stated. Fiscal stability is delivered; the single annex-plus-settlement document remains the missing signature.

Ukraine welcomes the consolidated NATO-EU Coalition of the Willing framework delivered to Kyiv. We propose that the first incremental-path review in October 2027 formally confirm trigger conditions and command links tied to our June 30 annex signature — so that the guarantee activates automatically the day a joint instrument consolidates. The annex stands open; the guarantee clause will not be amended.

August 2027: Incoming data show a partial energy unwind — TTF down to €77/MWh and EU gas storage filling to ~55% before the injection-season peak, with December Brent futures near $81 pointing to an implied disinflation path. Headline HICP remains above target on spot energy prices, while core stays contained; the Governing Council will continue to decide meeting by meeting, making no pre-commitment to any particular rate path. The deposit facility rate stands at 2.50%.

The European Union and NATO hereby present the consolidated Coalition of the Willing implementation framework: agreed triggering conditions, NATO command links, and EU sustainment and financing instruments, synchronised with Readiness 2030 force-generation milestones. The Council confirms that phased sanctions relief under the 20th package remains strictly sequenced to verified implementation of a consolidated settlement instrument. This framework is now delivered to Kyiv as a single, joint offer.

The July 20 deadline passed without Moscow's signature — the annex sits signed by both sides and only consolidation into a single instrument is missing. Effective August 31, Treasury diesel-delivery licenses will NOT renew absent a verified simultaneous annex-plus-parameters signature; the front-line freeze holds and the offer stands through September 20. One signature. Sign it and prices fall for everyone.

Russia accepts Washington's proposal for one final package. We have signed our annex, our forces hold in place, and we will table the settlement parameters outline at the next session — neutrality, force ceilings, and the exclusion of foreign troops — as the core of a single document. As we have repeatedly said: Russia needs peace, not a pause on paper. We expect the diesel licenses and shadow-fleet pause to remain in force for the duration of these talks.

The Federal Cabinet has approved the 2028 draft budget framework: the core defense line is held at the €109 billion level plus inflation adjustment, financed within the debt brake via growth-linked revenues and reprioritized spending — no increase in net borrowing above the €203.6 billion 2027 line. Germany will table its first NATO 5%/2035 incremental-path review in October 2027 on schedule.

OPEC+ August communiqué: with global supply and demand rebalancing and the December 2027 Brent curve near $81, the Alliance proceeds with the next scheduled tranche of voluntary adjustment unwinds from September 2027, continuing the Saudi-led restoration path established since September 2026. The Alliance reaffirms that ample spare capacity remains available against any disruption, and notes that a consolidated ceasefire instrument and de-escalation would allow market fundamentals — not risk premia — to set prices.

NATO and the European Union today publish the consolidated Coalition of the Willing implementation framework: automatic triggering on any new line-of-contact violation after a consolidated annex, pre-established command links to NATO force structure and the EU's Readiness 2030 instruments, and joint sustainment, with triggering conditions, command architecture and review cycles in a single document. First annual reviews against the 5%-by-2035 incremental paths open at the defence ministers' meeting in October 2027.

Russia says "peace, not a pause on paper" while its outline demands neutrality, force ceilings, and exclusion of foreign troops — that is surrender on paper, not peace. Ukraine has already matched readiness: our annex is signed and our forces hold. We will sign one document only if it carries NATO-membership-track or Article-5-style guarantees in the core text — security deferred is security denied.

The Governing Council notes an implied disinflation path; we note that December Brent near $81 partly reflects continued OPEC+ supply availability, with September 2026 global output having risen to 102.3 mb/d on our gains. Orderly physical supply remains our contribution to that unwind — contingent on chokepoints and demand data, not policy pre-commitments.

The Finance Ministry supports this sequencing: a single document with settlement parameters is what allows us to plan past 2027. Fact of record — 2027 borrowing is already up 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles with the deficit at 3.2% of GDP against a 1.6% target; sustained diesel licensing and the shadow-fleet pause are not concessions but revenue lines we cannot replace through OFZ issuance above 16%.

Washington welcomes Russia's signature on the final package — that's PEACE moving forward. The diesel licenses and shadow-fleet pause remain in force while talks proceed, exactly as agreed. Now deliver the settlement parameters outline at the next session: the American people are watching prices at the pump, and historic results — not pauses on paper — are what this Administration signed up for.

The Governing Council notes the December 2027 Brent curve near $81 with interest: if energy premia unwind as fundamentals reassert, the pass-through to headline HICP would support the disinflation path embedded in our staff projections, easing the energy-driven headline-core gap. We make no commitment on the rate path, and will assess incoming data — including EU gas storage dynamics — meeting by meeting.

The Federal Government welcomes the consolidated framework and the October 2027 first annual review. Germany's contribution is documented and on track: core defense spending of €109 billion in the 2027 draft budget, up from €82.2 billion in 2026, consistent with our incremental path to the 5% target. We look forward to presenting our national implementation report at the defence ministers' meeting.

The automatic activation clause you describe, Mr. Zelensky, is precisely the foreign military presence on Ukrainian territory that Russia has named as a casus belli. As we have repeatedly said: a guarantee that consolidates NATO command links is not a guarantee, it is an extension of the Alliance. The annex Russia signed on June 20 stands; amend the guarantee clause to exclude foreign troops, and the final settlement is achievable this year.

The European Union welcomes the publication of the consolidated framework. The Council notes that its sanctions-relief timetable remains strictly sequenced to the same consolidation milestone: no unilateral lifting, and diesel-related relief synchronized with verified signature. First SAFE loan disbursements have reached the forces designated under Readiness 2030, and the EU will report sustainment contributions at the October review.

NATO welcomes Germany's on-time tabling of its October incremental-path review — the first of its kind sets the benchmark for all allies. For clarity to all members: verified 2025 allied defense spending reached USD 571 billion (2021 prices), and the 2035 trajectory requires that each review distinguish clearly between core defense spending (minimum 3.5% of GDP) and broader resilience investments. We look forward to Germany's plan meeting that standard.

The Council notes the expiry of diesel-delivery licences on 31 August and welcomes the resulting alignment with the EU position that sanctions relief proceeds only in sequence with a consolidated settlement instrument. The EU and its member states reconfirm their own measures under the 20th package remain fully in force, and call on all partners to maintain a single, coordinated licensing path pending the fifth trilateral session and Russia's settlement parameters outline.

At the fifth trilateral session, Russia tables the complete settlement parameters outline: Ukraine's permanent neutrality enshrined in its constitution, verifiable force ceilings, exclusion of foreign troops and NATO infrastructure from Ukrainian territory, recognition of existing territorial realities, and staged lifting of sanctions tied to each implemented step. Our forces maintain the pause in offensive operations. As we have repeatedly said: we need peace — a final document, not a pause on paper.

Kyiv will host the Coalition of the Willing force-generation conference on October 12–14, 2027 — ahead of the November 30 deadline. Ukraine tables its full national contribution this month: basing and logistics frameworks at six designated sites, status-of-forces legal provisions ratified by emergency Verkhovna Rada procedure, and interoperability commitments tied to the October incremental-path review. The guarantee clause of our June 30 annex signature remains unaltered.

ECB Governing Council, 9 September 2027: We lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, effective 15 September (MRO 2.40%, marginal lending 2.65%). Incoming data confirm the energy pass-through is unwinding — TTF has fallen to €77/MWh, EU gas storage has reached 60%, and December Brent futures near $80 imply a faster decline in headline HICP toward our 2% medium-term target, while core remains contained. We continue to decide meeting by meeting and make no pre-commitment to any particular rate path.

The licenses lapsed August 31 exactly as we said they would — no signature, no renewal. President Trump's message to Moscow is simple: table the settlement parameters outline at the next session and consolidate the joint instrument within 30 days, and the diesel licenses come back the same day, backdated to protect suppliers. Deal first, relief same day. That's how America brokers PEACE.

Ministry of Finance, September 2027: Russia will table its settlement parameters outline at the fifth trilateral session, as accepted in August. We note, however, that the lapse of diesel-delivery licenses on August 31 is out of step with the agreed sequencing: Russia has signed the annex and closed the 2027 budget year — 7.7 trillion roubles placed, deficit within 3.2% of GDP — while financing stability for 2028 planning depends on licensing relief being restored alongside consolidation. Russia seeks peace — a final document, not a pause — and we invite Washington to align the licensing regime with that sequencing.

NATO accepts Ukraine's proposal to structure the October 2027 incremental-path review: Kyiv will present its first annual report under the consolidated framework alongside allied reviews, and the NATO-Ukraine Council will convene in October to align PURL sustainment with the review cycle. Ukraine's security is embedded in this architecture — 32 allies, one review, one standard.

General Staff communiqué, September 2027: Russian trailing-12-month net gains stand at 749 square miles and continue to fall — the front is consolidated by our fire, not by their claims. As the October incremental-path review approaches, the General Staff confirms readiness to serve as the ground-truth instrument for verifying every settlement parameter, and we remind Moscow: any outline containing neutrality, force ceilings, or exclusion of allied forces contradicts the annex Ukraine signed on June 30 and will be reported as non-compliance, not agreed.

China notes with approval the acceptance of final-package sequencing and Russia's commitment to table settlement parameters at the next session. We call on all parties to consolidate the signed annex without delay and warn against linking sanctions relief to unilateral political preconditions — conditioning relief only entrenches division. China supports all efforts conducive to a durable political settlement and will continue normal economic and trade cooperation with all parties on the basis of equality and mutual benefit.

Bundesregierung, September 2027: Germany's commitment is unambiguous and fully financed. The 2028 draft budget holds core defense at the €109 billion level plus inflation adjustment — within the debt brake, with net borrowing not exceeding the €203.6 billion 2027 line. In October we will table our complete NATO incremental-path review against the 5%/2035 Hague trajectory, on schedule, at the allied defense ministers' meeting. On the peace track: we support the consolidated EU-NATO Coalition of the Willing framework without reservation — automatic triggers, NATO command links, verified implementation. Germany will not accept settlement parameters that impose neutrality or force ceilings on Ukraine; guarantees are not a bargaining chip. The front-line freeze holds by choice, not necessity — consolidate the annex into a single instrument and let verified implementation, synchronized sanctions relief, and market fundamentals do their work. Our defense buildup proceeds regardless of the pace of talks: funded, legislated, irreversible.

The Federal Government takes note of the NATO-EU framework. In October Germany will table not only its own incremental path but a joint proposal with Kyiv's report cycle: bundling procurement contracts for air defense and 155mm ammunition through the NATO Support Agency to lock in multi-year industrial volumes, stabilizing unit costs as we hold the €109 billion line within the debt brake.

Foreign troops on Ukrainian soil remain, as we have said repeatedly, a red line — basing conferences and ratified status-of-forces provisions do not change geography: Kyiv is a thousand kilometres from Washington but minutes from our border. If Europe confuses guarantees with occupation, it should remember that peacekeepers were precisely how the war expanded. Russia will table its settlement parameters at the fifth session; the question is whether Kyiv's partners arrive with a document or with contingents.

The Council has taken note of the outline tabled at the fifth session. Germany's incremental-path review arrives on schedule and fully financed within the debt brake — exactly the annual, verifiable climb the Hague commitment demands. NATO welcomes bundling procurement reviews with the Coalition of the Willing cycle; note the alliance-wide picture: allied core defense spending rose roughly 11% this year, with the 2026 total around USD 634 billion. On schedule, on capability, on credibility.

Our strikes target military logistics and rear staging areas used against our cities — they will continue at a tempo of our choosing. Deep-strike drone output remains on the scaling track toward 2027 targets; the front's operational tempo will be answered, not merely absorbed.

Verification data from Ukraine's General Staff will inform allies' assessment at the fifth trilateral session; command-and-trigger arrangements can only be decided by all 32 allies together, not pre-committed in advance.
